title: Security, administration and observability
scope:
This category covers security, administration and observability of the C++ MDS, from four map pages: [auth-and-mds-caps](../cpp-map/01-cluster-integration/auth-and-mds-caps.md) (MDS self-authentication, peer authentication, the `mds` cap language and its evaluation, every enforcement point, client-side checks through `cap_auths`, and how the monitor and mgr generate caps), [admin-commands](../cpp-map/13-admin-and-config/admin-commands.md) (the admin socket and `tell` transports, their authorization, parsing and output conventions, and all 60 MDS commands plus the generic ones with their callers), [config-perf-counters-and-health](../cpp-map/13-admin-and-config/config-perf-counters-and-health.md) (the option framework, perf counters and their export, beacon health metrics, cluster log and task status) and [mgr-tools-and-orchestration](../cpp-map/01-cluster-integration/mgr-tools-and-orchestration.md) (every mgr module, orchestrator and tool that talks to the MDS or to CephFS).

Admin commands that drive subsystems owned by other categories (scrub, damage, export, fragmentation, lock manager, quiesce, quarantine, QoS) are catalogued here only as command surfaces, with links to the owning map pages. Individual configuration options are catalogued with the mechanism they tune by the owning category; this category holds the framework, the options read by peers, and test-only options. For each admin command, counter, health check and option the entries record which callers depend on the name and output format (mgr modules, cephadm, Rook, ceph-exporter, qa, operators).

Excluded and owned elsewhere: transport and cephx as clients see them, client feature bits, session lifecycle and eviction semantics (category 02-client-sessions-and-protocol); FSMap, beacons, standby affinity (`mds_join_fs`) and beacon/heartbeat options (category 01-cluster-membership-and-ha); vxattr handling (category 04-namespace-and-posix-operations); cache, journal, balancer, purge/scrub and QoS/metrics options and mechanisms (categories 05, 06, 07, 09, 10).

Cross-category review (2026-10-11): entries that duplicated an entry of the owning category were retired (listed under "retired" in features.json with the entry they were merged into) or shortened to pointers whose description starts with "See F-XXX-NNN." and keeps only the facts specific to this category.

features.name: MDS self-authentication, keyring and rotating service secrets
features.summary: The MDS authenticates to the monitors as `mds.<id>` and obtains service tickets and rotating `mds` secrets so that it can talk to mons, OSDs, peer MDSs and the mgr and verify client authorizers.
features.description: `MDSDaemon::init` sets `want_keys` to MON|OSD|MDS|MGR, installs the `MonClient` as the messenger's AuthClient and AuthServer, calls `authenticate()` and then `wait_auth_rotating(rotating_keys_bootstrap_timeout)` up to `max_rotating_auth_attempts` times; failure of either step calls `suicide()`. The default `keyring` for an MDS is `$mds_data/keyring` (`/var/lib/ceph/mds/$cluster-$id/keyring`), set by `common_preinit`; without a loadable key cephx is dropped from the supported methods and init fails with `-ENOENT` unless `none` is configured. The monitor hands out three rotating secrets per service (previous, current, next); the MDS keeps only the last set and requests a new one when fewer than three are held or the current one expired at least `min(30 s, auth_service_ticket_ttl/4)` ago. Methods and modes towards mon/mgr follow `auth_cluster_required` and `ms_mon_cluster_mode`, towards MDS/OSD `auth_cluster_required` and `ms_cluster_mode`, towards clients `auth_service_required` and `ms_service_mode`. The peers enforce the MDS entity's own caps: deployed as `mon 'profile mds'` (beacons need `mds` X, eviction needs `osd blocklist`, `MRemoveSnaps` needs `osd pool rmsnap`), `osd 'allow rw tag cephfs *=*'` and `mds 'allow'` (a peer MDS refuses a connection whose `mds` cap is missing).
features.notes: cephadm writes the keyring into the daemon data directory mounted at `/var/lib/ceph/mds/ceph-<id>`; Rook passes `--keyring=/etc/ceph/keyring-store/keyring` explicitly, gives the MDS `osd 'allow *'` instead of the `cephfs` tag, and with AES256K support the key and rotating secrets are `aes256k` (rook f190ca3b45f; see the mgr-tools page 3.9.3). The mgr accepts MDS connections even with empty mgr caps (`DaemonServer::ms_handle_fast_authentication`). See also F-PROTO-012 (rotating secrets as clients depend on them), F-CLU-110 (MonClient session and subscriptions).

features.name: Peer authorizer verification and caps loading at connection accept
features.summary: Every connecting peer is authenticated with a cephx authorizer for service type MDS, and the `mds` caps carried in its ticket become the session's `auth_caps`.
features.description: The authorizer itself is verified by `MonClient::handle_auth_request` with the rotating `mds` secret (F-PROTO-011). `MDSDaemon::ms_handle_fast_authentication` then parses the caps from the ticket on the messenger worker without `mds_lock` (`parse_caps`: allow_all -> allow-all, else decode one string and run `MDSAuthCaps::parse`); an entity with no `mds` cap (empty blob, decode throws) or an unparseable string refuses the connection with `-EACCES`, which the peer sees as BADAUTHORIZER (msgr1) or `AUTH_BAD_METHOD` (msgr2) (or `_exit(auth_exit_on_failure)` when that option is >= 0). `ms_handle_accept` then finds the existing `Session` for `entity_name_t(peer_type, global_id)` or creates a closed one (also on a rank-less daemon, so that `allow *` peers can run tell commands) and parses the caps again into `Session::auth_caps`. The caps are a snapshot taken when the ticket was issued; they are never persisted: `session_info_t` keeps only `auth_name`, and sessions loaded from the SessionMap or created by import have empty caps until the client connects.
features.notes: Caps refresh only with a new `Connection` object: a msgr2 reconnect merged by `ProtocolV2::reuse_connection` (stateful_server policy) moves the socket and `auth_meta` but not `peer_caps_info`, so `ms_handle_accept` re-parses the old caps (code reading, not reproduced; src/msg/async/ProtocolV2.cc:2814). The kclient on `AUTH_BAD_METHOD` invalidates its MDS ticket and returns `-EACCES` (linux/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:7363 (mds_handle_auth_bad_method)). The transport and handshake themselves belong to category 02-client-sessions-and-protocol. No code compares the claimed entity type with the type of the authenticated EntityName (transport page 3.2). MCommand (ceph tell) on a client connection requires auth_caps.allow_all() (F-ADM-028). See also F-PROTO-011 (authorizer), F-PROTO-015 (connection-to-session binding).

legacy_parts.note: The msgr1 refusal path: -EACCES from ms_handle_fast_authentication answered with CEPH_MSGR_TAG_BADAUTHORIZER by ProtocolV1::handle_connect_message_2. The gates cephx_require_signatures and cephx_service_require_version, which the accepting daemon evaluates only in ProtocolV1::handle_connect_message_2, where they add CEPH_FEATURE_MSG_AUTH and CEPH_FEATUREMASK_CEPHX_V2 to the msgr1 required features. Only a peer connected over msgr1 receives the refusal as BADAUTHORIZER and is subject to the signature and cephx-version gates. The 7.3 kernel mounted by mount.ceph with the new device syntax runs with ms_mode=prefer-crc, and Ceph clients and daemons at this commit connect to the first usable address of the MDS addrvec, which daemons publish v2 first, so a refused baseline peer receives AUTH_BAD_METHOD over msgr2. Message signatures exist only in ProtocolV1; the kernel's msgr1 default applies only to the old device syntax or an explicit ms_mode=legacy.
evidence_notes: grep of src: cephx_require_signatures, cephx_service_require_signatures and cephx_*require_version are read only in src/msg/async/ProtocolV1.cc and src/mon/AuthMonitor.cc

features.name: Authentication method none (and Kerberos) means allow-all
features.summary: Without cephx for clients, every client peer is treated as holding `mds 'allow *'`, including for tell commands.
features.description: With `auth_service_required = none`, `AuthNoneAuthorizeHandler::verify_authorizer` sets `AuthCapsInfo::allow_all = true`; `MDSDaemon::parse_caps` then calls `MDSAuthCaps::set_allow_all()`, which installs one grant with spec `ALL` and an empty match. The Kerberos handler does the same (`KrbAuthorizeHandler.cpp:50`). The entity name and global id are taken from the peer's unauthenticated claim. Daemon peers follow `auth_cluster_required`. Under cephx a service ticket never carries `allow_all` (`cephx_verify_authorizer` rejects it).

features.name: Peer-type message filtering and rank address check
features.summary: Security view of message filtering: which peer may send what, and what is not bound to the authenticated identity.
features.description: See F-CLU-115 (dispatch and peer-type filtering) and F-CLU-072 (stale peer messages). Security-relevant facts: MSG_COMMAND is not type-filtered (it is gated by allow_all()); client session, reconnect, reclaim, caps, cap-release and lease messages are accepted only from CLIENT peers; CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_REQUEST is not type-filtered, but a session is attached only when req->is_a_client(), and Server::check_access is a no-op for session-less requests; inter-rank messages are accepted only from MDS peers whose rank is up and only on the connection to that rank's MDSMap address. The MDS never forwards an MClientRequest itself (it sends MClientRequestForward to the client), so each request is evaluated against the caps of the connection it arrived on.
features.notes: Peer type and message source are not bound to the authenticated entity: on the accepting side `ProtocolV2::handle_hello` takes the peer type from the HELLO frame and the source from CLIENT_IDENT; no comparison with the authenticated `peer_name`/`peer_global_id` was found (code search; not reproduced; auth page section 8 item 25).

features.name: Daemon key rotation commands (rotate-key, wipe-rotating-secrets)
features.summary: The MDS process accepts a new cephx key for its own entity through an admin command; cephadm has a (currently uncalled) rotation path that uses it.
features.description: `MonClient::init` registers the asok/tell commands `rotate-key` (input buffer = base64 key, added for the daemon's own entity to the in-memory keyring; `-EINVAL` on decode failure or without cephx) and `wipe-rotating-secrets`. The tell is subject to the `allow *` gate. The monitor side of a rotation is `auth get-or-create-pending` / `auth commit-pending`. cephadm's `_rotate_daemon_key` (pending key, keyring rewrite, `rotate-key` tell, restart on failure) has no caller at this commit: `ceph orch daemon rotate-key` fails with "key rotation by orchestrator not supported in this release". Rook rotates with the mon command `auth rotate`, rewrites the keyring Secret and restarts the pod; it never sends `rotate-key`.
features.notes: During a cephadm upgrade an MDS named in `AUTH_INSECURE_SERVICE_KEY_TYPE` gets its key rotated with `mgr.key_rotate` before redeploy (src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/upgrade.py:1917-1975).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: MDS cap string grammar, parser and canonical forms
features.summary: Parses the `mds` cap string of an entity into grants; the monitor validates cap strings with the same C++ parser, so the accepted language is shared.
features.description: Grammar (Boost.Spirit, no skipper inside): grants `allow <spec> [fsname=F] [path=P] [root_squash] [uid=N] [gids=a,b,...] [network CIDR]` separated by `,` or `;` with only spaces around the separator; `spec` is `*`, `all`, or `r` followed by optional `w f p Q q s` in exactly this order; qualifiers in exactly this order; the complete string `allow` (byte-exact) means `allow rwps`. Keywords are case-sensitive; unquoted paths are limited to `[a-zA-Z0-9_./-]`, quoted paths cannot contain their quote character; `fsname=*` is not expressible; `uid` is a 32-bit unsigned decimal; `network` is separated by a space, not `=`. On failure all grants are cleared and the error text is "Permission flags in MDS capability string must be '*' or 'all' or must start with 'r'" (remainder contains `allow`) or "mds capability parse failed, stopped at '<rest>' of '<str>'". `operator<<` prints `allow <spec>[ fsname=F][ path="/P"][ root_squash][ uid=U[ gids=..]][ network N]`; `to_string()` (used by the monitor's merge) prints the path without leading slash and quotes and omits `network`.
features.notes: Whitespace quirks confirmed in a standalone harness against Boost 1.83: leading/trailing `ascii::space` of the whole string is skipped (`" allow r "` parses) but `" allow"` and `"allow "` fail because the legacy compare is byte-exact. `gids=` without `uid=` parses and has no effect. Uids >= 2^31 parse but never match (caller uid compared as `int`). A bracketed IPv6 network parses but yields an unusable grant. With `mon_auth_validate_all_caps=false` an invalid string can enter the auth database and is then refused by the MDS at connection time.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: Grant evaluation: union of grants in a fixed step order
features.summary: Decides whether a request with a given access mask on an inode is allowed for a session; any passing grant allows, otherwise the client gets `-EACCES`.
features.description: `MDSAuthCaps::is_capable` iterates grants in string order: (1) skip if the grant has a network and the session address is outside it or the network is invalid; (2) skip unless fs name, uid/gids and path match; (3) skip unless the spec allows the read/execute and write bits of the mask; (4) if a quarantine check is requested and the grant lacks `q`/`Q`, return false immediately; (5) skip a `root_squash` grant for `MAY_WRITE` when caller uid or gid is 0; (6) skip if `MAY_SET_VXATTR`, `MAY_SNAPSHOT` or `MAY_FULL` is requested and the grant lacks `p`, `s` or `f`; (7) allow if the grant uid is ANY; (8) otherwise apply the chown/chgrp rules and the owner/group/other mode-bit test. There are no deny grants; only step 4 makes the result order-dependent. Mask bits: `MAY_READ` 1, `MAY_WRITE` 2, `MAY_EXECUTE` 4 (never requested), `MAY_CHOWN` 16, `MAY_CHGRP` 32, `MAY_SET_VXATTR` 64, `MAY_SNAPSHOT` 128, `MAY_FULL` 256. Spec `*`/`all` implies `r w f p s` but never `q`/`Q`.
features.notes: Evaluation is a pure function of (session caps, inode path, inode uid/gid/mode, caller credentials, mask, peer address). Worked examples and the unit tests (`src/test/mds/TestMDSAuthCaps.cc`) are on the auth page section 3.5. Clients evaluate the exported `cap_auths` with different semantics (last matching grant wins, no match allows), see F-ADM-021.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: path= restriction and the inode path used for checks
features.summary: Restricts a grant to a subtree; the MDS compares the inode's primary path from the file-system root with the grant path.
features.description: At parse time all leading `/` of the grant path are stripped; trailing `/` are ignored by `match_path`; an empty path (also `path=/` or `path=""`) matches everything; otherwise the inode path must equal the grant path or continue with `/` (`path=/foo` matches `foo`, `foo/d`, not `food`). Inner `//`, `.` and `..` are not normalized. `Session::check_access` builds the projected primary-parent path with `make_path_string` and strips the leading `/`; for an inode whose parent is a stray directory it uses the inode's `stray_prior_path` (set at unlink and when rename unlinks a target), and the parent's `stray_prior_path` when the grandparent is a stray (inode inside a deleted snapshotted directory). The uid, gid and mode compared later come from the committed (non-projected) inode. Access through a remote (hard) link is judged by the primary link's path.
features.notes: mgr/volumes (`allow r|rw path=<subvolume data path>`), mgr/nfs (`allow rw path=<export path>`) and `ceph fs authorize` all produce path grants. The path is the only non-local input of the check, so a rename of any ancestor changes the result.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: fsname= restriction and file-system gating of session messages
features.summary: Restricts a grant to one file system and refuses session traffic for file systems the entity has no grant for.
features.description: `MDSCapMatch::match_fs` treats `""` or `"*"` as any file system. `fs_name_capable(fs, MAY_READ)` (true for `allow_all()` or any grant for the fs whose spec allows read; ignores path, uid and network) is checked for every `MClientSession` when the MDSMap has an fs name: on failure the MDS sends `CEPH_SESSION_REJECT` with `metadata["error_string"] = client doesn't have caps for FS "<fs>"` directly on the connection. `MClientReclaim` failing the same test is silently dropped. libcephfs surfaces a REJECT as `-EPERM` ("Operation not permitted" at mount); the kclient fails later requests with `-EACCES` unless mounted with `recover_session=clean`.
features.notes: `ceph fs rename` does not rewrite `fsname=` caps and requires `--yes-i-really-mean-it` because "clients' cephx credentials need reauthorized" (src/mon/FSCommands.cc:1336). Reconnect messages are not fs-name checked (`Server::handle_client_reconnect`). The kclient compares fs names with `ceph_namespace_match` (`NULL`, `""`, `"*"` match any).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: uid=/gids= restriction with simplified mode-bit check
features.summary: Limits a grant to an asserted caller uid (and groups) and then checks the inode's owner/group/other permission bits for that caller.
features.description: A grant with `uid=N` matches only requests whose `caller_uid` equals N and, if `gids` are given, whose `caller_gid` or a supplementary gid (from `MClientRequest` `gid_list`) is listed. After the flag checks, the class is owner if `inode_uid == caller_uid`, else group if `inode_gid` is in the grant gids held by the caller, else other; the class's r/w/x bits must cover the mask. `MAY_CHOWN` requires `new_uid == caller_uid` and `inode_uid == caller_uid` (never both true, because setattr adds `MAY_CHOWN` only when the uid changes, so a uid grant never allows chown); `MAY_CHGRP` requires ownership and a new gid in the effective gid set. The caller identity is asserted by the client and not verified by the MDS. Open for write requests `MAY_READ` too (except an `O_TRUNC` open), and getattr/lookup need `MAY_READ` on the target.
features.notes: `uid=0` is stored as -1 (any), so a grant cannot be restricted to root. `std::set_intersection` assumes a sorted `caller_gid_list`, which the MDS uses as received (kclient lists are sorted; libcephfs and Ganesha lists are passed as supplied, unverified whether sorted). No mgr module or orchestrator generates `uid=` grants (none found in the map pages).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: root_squash grants
features.summary: A `root_squash` grant cannot be used for writes by callers with uid 0 or gid 0.
features.description: In `is_capable` step 5, a grant with `root_squash` is skipped (not denied) when `caller_uid == 0` or `caller_gid == 0` and the mask contains `MAY_WRITE`; another grant may still allow. Vxattr operations request only `MAY_SET_VXATTR` (no `MAY_WRITE`), so `allow rwp root_squash` lets root set quotas, layouts and pins. `root_squash_in_caps(fs)` feeds the broken-root_squash health check, and the flag is exported to clients in `cap_auths` for client-side enforcement of cached operations. `ceph fs authorize ... root_squash` and the dashboard generate it; the monitor's merge can add `root_squash` to a grant but never remove it.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: p flag: permission to set ceph.* vxattrs and non-default layouts
features.summary: Gates changes of layouts, quotas, pins, subvolume flags, charmap and quiesce-block vxattrs.
features.description: `MAY_SET_VXATTR` is requested (alone, without `MAY_WRITE`) by `handle_client_setvxattr` for SETXATTR/RMXATTR of `is_ceph_vxattr` names (`ceph.dir.layout*`, `ceph.file.layout*`, `ceph.quota*`, `ceph.quiesce.block`, `ceph.dir.subvolume`, `ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible`, `ceph.dir.pin`, `.pin.random`, `.pin.distributed`, `ceph.dir.charmap`, `.normalization`, `.encoding`, `.casesensitive`). It is added to `MAY_WRITE` for SETLAYOUT/SETDIRLAYOUT that change the layout and for CREATE whose requested stripe unit/count, object size or pool differ from the inherited layout. A failing grant is skipped; with no passing grant the request gets `-EACCES`.
features.notes: `allow rp` (accepted by the MDS grammar, rejected by `ceph fs authorize`) can set layouts, quotas and pins without write permission. mgr/volumes and mgr/mirroring rely on their mounts holding `p` (mgr has `allow *`; mirror bootstrap generates `rwps`).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: s flag and snapshot uid range
features.summary: Gates mksnap, rmsnap and renamesnap; a separate uid range option gates all snapshot-modifying ops.
features.description: MKSNAP (0x1400), RMSNAP (0x1401) and RENAMESNAP (0x1403) call `check_access(MAY_WRITE|MAY_SNAPSHOT)` on the directory; before that, a caller uid outside [`mds_snap_min_uid`, `mds_snap_max_uid`] returns `-EPERM`. SNAP_METADATA (0x1406) applies only the uid range and has no caps check, so an `allow r` client (the cephfs-mirror daemon) can update snapshot metadata. LSSNAP and READDIR_SNAPDIFF request `MAY_READ`.
features.notes: Snapshot semantics themselves (realms, snap ids, limits) belong to category 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes. See also F-SNAP-020 (uid range option).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: f flag: metadata-pool-full bypass
features.summary: The f flag of an MDS cap grant bypasses the metadata-pool-full gate.
features.description: See F-STORE-099. Auth-cap specifics: a grant with f (or *) satisfies the MAY_FULL check that dispatch_client_request makes on the request's base inode while the metadata pool is full; without it the request fails (clients see -EACCES from check_access). The f bypass does not apply to a SETATTR that grows a file while full, which returns -ENOSPC regardless.
features.notes: `ceph fs authorize` cannot generate `f` ("Unknown permission flag 'f'"). Double reply derived from code reading, not reproduced.

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: q/Q flags: access to quarantined subtrees
features.summary: Grants with `q` or `Q` keep access to quarantined subvolumes; other quarantine-aware sessions are denied there.
features.description: For clients advertising `CEPHFS_FEATURE_QUARANTINE`, `Server::check_access` passes `check_qtine = in->is_under_quarantine()`; the first grant that matches fs, path, uid and r/w but lacks `q`/`Q` returns false (`-EACCES`) without consulting later grants. `quarantine_access_in_caps(fs, path)` is evaluated by `Locker::issue_new_caps`/`issue_caps` for each client cap on every issue, restricting caps on quarantined inodes. `Q` is documented as access to all quarantined subtrees but is evaluated exactly like `q` (limited by the grant path). Neither is implied by `*`/`all`.
features.notes: The inode path is built for every cap issue even without quarantine (only the `EQUARANTINED` errno path is gated on `is_under_quarantine()`). The quarantine mechanism itself belongs to category 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine. Grammar: after r the optional letters come in the fixed order w f p Q q s (for example rwq, rwQ, rq, rwfpQqs) and are printed in that order; in MDSCapSpec Q = 1<<6 and Q_PRIME = 1<<7. For requests, MDSAuthCaps::is_capable lets the first grant that matches network, fs, path, uid and r/w decide; for caps, quarantine_access_in_caps is true if any grant with a matching fs name has q or Q and a path equal to the inode path or an ancestor, ignoring uid/gid, network and root_squash. First-match pitfall: with "allow rw, allow rwq path=/volumes/_nogroup/sv", requests on sv get -EACCES (the first grant lacks q) while issue_caps grants full caps. The monitor validates cap strings with the same parser and distributes them in tickets. See also F-QOS-071 (EACCES for aware sessions), F-QOS-074 (cap restriction).

features.group: MDS auth caps: language and evaluation
features.name: network restriction
features.summary: A grant with `network A/P` applies only to sessions whose peer address lies inside that CIDR.
features.description: The session's `info.inst.addr` is tested with `network_contains` (same address family required); `parse_network` needs `addr/prefix` accepted by `inet_pton`, and a grant whose network does not parse is unusable in `is_capable`. The network is ignored by `allow_all()` (tell and fscrypt gates), `fs_name_capable` and `path_capable`, and is dropped by `to_string()`, so a `ceph fs authorize` merge loses it.
features.notes: Unit test `network`: `allow * network 192.168.0.0/16, allow * network 10.0.0.0/8` denies a client at 192.167.2.3.

features.name: Mount root check at session open and auth_name check at reclaim
features.summary: At `REQUEST_OPEN` the client-claimed mount root must be covered by some grant path; reclaiming another session requires the same cephx entity.
features.description: In `handle_client_session` for `CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_OPEN`, after the `refuse_client_session`, blocklist and required-feature checks and the root_squash detection, a `root` metadata key (if present) must start with `/` and satisfy `path_capable` (a textual prefix test that ignores fs name, spec and network); failure sends `CEPH_SESSION_REJECT` with `error_string` `invalue root '<root>'` (sic) or `non-allowable root '<root>'` (only to clients with `CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC`) and clog warning `client session with ... denied`. The kclient sends `root` = mount server path or `/`; libcephfs sends its mount root (`/` by default) but omits the key outside `mount` (`mds_command` on an unmounted client, `start_reclaim`), which skips the check. `Server::reclaim_session` refuses with `MClientReclaimReply` result `-EPERM` when `session->info.auth_name` differs from the target's; `auth_name` is persisted in `session_info_t` and `ESession` for this purpose.
features.notes: The root test is a convenience gate (`/a/../b` passes `path=/a`); reconnect re-checks neither fs name nor root. Caps `allow r fsname=a path=/a, allow rw fsname=b path=/b` let a client open a session on fs `a` with root `/b`, after which every checked operation is denied. Session state machinery belongs to category 02-client-sessions-and-protocol. See also F-PROTO-029 (session open admission).

legacy_parts.note: REJECT for an invalid or non-allowable root sent to a session without CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8): send_reject_message omits error_string, so MClientSession is encoded as header v1. Sessions without CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8) come only from kernels up to v4.18 and Ceph clients up to 13.2.1, whose feature sets are inferred and never include bit 8. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs at this commit advertise bit 8, so a refused root reaches them as a header-v7 REJECT that carries error_string.
evidence: linux-v4.18/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:953 (create_session_open_msg, session v2 without feature bits)

features.name: Per-request access-check matrix
features.summary: Defines which inode and which mask each client operation is checked against, and which operations are not checked.
features.description: `Server::check_access(mdr, in, mask)` is a no-op without a session, else calls `Session::check_access`, which returns `-EIO` for a directory whose layout has a pool namespace when the connection lacks `CEPH_FEATURE_FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2`, then `-EACCES` if `is_capable` fails. Targets and masks: LOOKUP/GETATTR/LOOKUPSNAP `MAY_READ` on the target; LOOKUPINO/HASH/PARENT/NAME mask 0 on the target (match only) then `MAY_READ` on the parent if locks were requested; OPEN `MAY_READ` plus `MAY_WRITE` for write modes (`O_TRUNC` checks `MAY_WRITE` only); CREATE/MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK `MAY_WRITE` on the parent; READDIR `MAY_READ`; SETATTR `MAY_WRITE` (+`MAY_CHOWN`/`MAY_CHGRP` when uid/gid change); SETXATTR of non-ceph names `MAY_WRITE`; LINK target and destination dir, UNLINK/RMDIR parent only, RENAME source dir, destination dir and source inode, each `MAY_WRITE` on the first pass only (skipped once peers witnessed). Not checked: RMXATTR of non-`ceph.*` names, GETVXATTR, SETFILELOCK/GETFILELOCK, FILE_BLOCKDIFF, SNAP_METADATA (uid range only). Most checks run after path traversal and lock acquisition, under `mds_lock`.
features.notes: Batched getattr/lookup (`mds_allow_batched_ops`): only the batch head runs `check_access`, and `Batch_Getattr_Lookup::_respond` sends its result and trace to followers from other sessions. Cap flushes (`MClientCaps` with dirty metadata) are not access-checked since commit 96305b5eef0. `Server::_check_access` is declared in Server.h:234 and never defined. The full table with line numbers is on the auth page section 3.7. See also F-QOS-071 (quarantine EACCES).

legacy_parts.note: The -EIO return of Session::check_access for a directory whose layout has a pool namespace when the connection lacks CEPH_FEATURE_FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2. The declaration Server::_check_access, which has no definition and no caller. A connection lacks CEPH_FEATURE_FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 (bit 58) only for kernels before v4.5 and Ceph clients before 10.2.0. The 7.3 kernel advertises bit 58 (under its aliases CRUSH_TUNABLES5 and NEW_OSDOPREPLY_ENCODING) in its msgr2 client ident, and libcephfs at this commit includes FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 in CEPH_FEATURES_ALL, so baseline sessions go straight to is_capable. Server::_check_access is declared in Server.h and is neither defined nor called in src/mds.
evidence_notes: grep of src/mds finds no definition or call)

features.name: fscrypt attribute changes require allow *
features.summary: Setting the fscrypt auth or file attributes through SETATTR is allowed only for sessions whose caps satisfy `allow_all()`.
features.description: After the regular `check_access(MAY_WRITE)` of SETATTR, a request carrying `CEPH_SETATTR_FSCRYPT_FILE` or `CEPH_SETATTR_FSCRYPT_AUTH` returns `-EACCES` unless `session->auth_caps.allow_all()` (a `*` grant without path and uid; fs name and network ignored). `fscrypt_auth`/`fscrypt_file` sent with a create are copied into the new inode in `prepare_new_inode` without this gate.
features.notes: mgr/volumes copies `ceph.fscrypt.auth`/`ceph.fscrypt.file` when creating clones; libcephfs turns those setxattrs into SETATTR with the fscrypt flags (mgr-tools page 3.1.4). See also F-NS-064, F-CACHE-009.

features.name: cap_auths export in CEPH_SESSION_OPEN and client-side checks
features.summary: Every session OPEN message carries a reduced copy of the session's grants so that clients can enforce read-only and root_squash for operations they complete from cached caps.
features.description: Each `MClientSession` with op `CEPH_SESSION_OPEN` carries `vector<MDSCapAuth>` in grant order: per grant `MDSCapMatch` v1 (s64 uid with -1 = any, u32 count + u32 gids, string path without leading `/`, string fs_name, u8 root_squash) plus u8 `readable` and u8 `writeable`, each struct with a 6-byte versioned header. It is on the wire only for message version >= 6, which is used when `metadata` or `supported_features` is non-empty (the MDS fills `supported_features` only for `CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC` clients); `HEAD_VERSION = 7` appends `oldest_client_tid`. Sent from `_session_logged`, the already-open re-notification (REQUEST_OPEN with `CEPHFS_FEATURE_NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE`), `finish_force_open_sessions` (import, rejoin, cross-MDS rename) and reconnect success. The kclient replaces its mount-wide list on every OPEN from any rank and checks `ceph_open`, `ceph_atomic_open` (parent path), unlink/rmdir/rmsnap and setattr; libcephfs checks `_do_setattr` and cap-satisfied `_open`. Client semantics: the last matching grant decides; no match allows; `p`, `s`, `f`, `q`, network and mode bits are unknown to clients.
features.notes: The kclient reads the fields positionally after skipping the 6-byte headers without using `len` (linux/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:4468-4527), so the v1 field layout is fixed for it. An OPEN built by `finish_force_open_sessions` before the client connected is queued with an empty list (imported sessions have empty `auth_caps`), which disables kclient checks until a later OPEN (derived from code reading). Example of the semantic split: caps `allow rw, allow r path=/ro` let the MDS allow writes in `/ro` while the kclient refuses write opens there. Client versions: Linux v6.10+, Ceph 18.2.4 and 19.2.0+ advertise bit 21; kernels v6.8-v6.9 already send session v7 but do not parse cap_auths, and an OPEN below v6 clears the kernel list. Because the kernel ignores struct_len here, any field appended to MDSCapAuth or MDSCapMatch desynchronizes every kernel that parses cap_auths (kclient expectations 8). libcephfs never tests the MDS bit 21, allows access locally when no grant matches or no list was sent, and sends cap flushes with caller_uid/gid -1. See also F-PROTO-031 (MClientSession encoding), F-ADM-022.

legacy_parts.note: OPEN sent to a session without CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8): all four OPEN send sites leave supported_features and metric_spec empty for such a session, so MClientSession::encode_payload emits header v1, which has no cap_auths field. Only kernels up to v4.18 and Ceph clients up to 13.2.1 open sessions without bit 8, so only they receive an OPEN without the feature bitmap and without cap_auths. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs at this commit advertise bit 8 and bit 21, so every OPEN they receive is header v7 and carries cap_auths.
evidence: linux-v4.18/fs/ceph/mds_client.c:953 (create_session_open_msg, session v2 without feature bits)

features.name: MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH health check
features.summary: Raises a HEALTH_ERR check for sessions whose caps use root_squash but whose client cannot enforce it locally.
features.description: At `REQUEST_OPEN` and at reconnect, a session whose caps contain `root_squash` for this fs and whose client lacks `CEPHFS_FEATURE_MDS_AUTH_CAPS_CHECK` (bit 21) is added to `SessionMap::broken_root_squash_clients`; the session is not rejected. `Beacon::notify_health` reports metric `MDS_HEALTH_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH` (id 15, check code `MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH`, HEALTH_ERR): one metric per client ("Client <name> has broken root_squash implementation", metadata `client_id`) or, above `mds_health_summarize_threshold` (10), one summary metric "There are N clients with broken root_squash implementations" (metadata `client_count`). Summary: "%num% MDS report clients with broken root_squash implementation". Entries are removed only by `SessionMap::remove_session`.
features.notes: The set holds raw `Session*`; a session added at REQUEST_OPEN and then rejected is never removed and may be dereferenced after free by the next `notify_health` (code reading, not reproduced; auth page section 8 item 17). Because the check is HEALTH_ERR and not on Rook's ignore list, it stops Rook's CephFilesystem reconcile while raised (mgr-tools page 3.9.2). Affected clients: kernels before v6.10 and Ceph clients before 18.2.4/19.2.0 (kclient expectations 7.1.2). See also F-ADM-021 (client-side checks), F-ADM-011 (root_squash).

legacy.note: The check is raised only for a session whose caps use root_squash on the file system and whose client lacks CEPHFS_FEATURE_MDS_AUTH_CAPS_CHECK (bit 21): Linux before v6.10 (including the CentOS Stream 8 sample) and Ceph clients before 18.2.4 and 19.2.0. The 7.3 kernel advertises bit 21, and libcephfs at this commit advertises CEPHFS_FEATURES_ALL for ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha V15.7, cephfs-mirror and the mgr modules, so no baseline client triggers it. Only the debug option client_debug_inject_features can remove the bit from libcephfs.
evidence_notes: git show v18.2.2/v18.2.4:src/mds/cephfs_features.h (bit 21 absent in 18.2.2, present in 18.2.4)

features.group: Caps provisioning by the monitor and mgr
features.name: ceph fs authorize: cap generation and merge on the monitor
features.summary: The monitor command that generates matching mon/mds/osd caps for a client and merges new grants into existing ones.
features.description: `ceph fs authorize <fs|*|all> <entity> <path> <perm> [root_squash] [<path> <perm> [root_squash] ...]`: unknown fs gives `-EINVAL`; perm characters must be strictly increasing ASCII except the leading `rw`, allowed `r w p s q Q` and `*` alone, `f` rejected. Generated strings: mon `allow r[ fsname=<fs>]`; mds `allow <perm>[ fsname=<fs>][ path=<path>][ root_squash]` per pair joined with `", "` (no `path=` for `/`, path unquoted); osd `allow r[w] tag cephfs data=<fs>`. All are validated with `MDSAuthCaps::parse` (mds and osd only while `mon_auth_validate_all_caps`), so a path needing quotes fails. For an existing entity, `MDSAuthCaps::merge` replaces the spec of a grant with the same (fs_name, path), can add but never remove `root_squash`, appends other grants, and rewrites the string with `to_string()` (dropping `network` and quotes); nothing changed gives "no update for caps of <entity>".
features.notes: Cannot express `p` together with `Q` (mon requires ASCII order `Q` < `p`, MDS grammar requires `p` before `Q`). A merge-time parse failure of stored caps (`CAPS_PARSING_ERR`) returns 0 with the error only in the status text (src/mon/AuthMonitor.cc:2012-2022). Users: dashboard (`fs authorize`, optional `root_squash`), mgr/mirroring bootstrap (`fs authorize <fs> client.<name> / rwps`).

features.group: Caps provisioning by the monitor and mgr
features.name: mgr/volumes subvolume authorize, deauthorize and authorized_list
features.summary: mgr/volumes creates or updates cephx users with path-restricted MDS caps for a subvolume and records them in files inside CephFS.
features.description: `fs subvolume authorize <vol> <sub> <auth_id> [--group_name] [--access_level r|rw] [--tenant_id] [--allow_existing_id]` builds mds `allow <r|rw> path=<subvolume data path>` (no `fsname=`), osd `allow <r|rw> pool=<ceph.dir.layout.pool>[ namespace=<pool_namespace>]`, mon `allow r`, and writes them with `auth get-or-create` or a string-level merge through `auth caps` (split on `,`, drop the opposite access level for the same path). Bookkeeping files `/volumes/$<auth_id>.meta` and `/volumes/_<group>:<subvol>.meta` hold JSON with dirty flags and are serialized with blocking libcephfs `flock(LOCK_EX)` plus an inode-equality recheck. `deauthorize` removes the grant and uses `auth rm` when no caps remain; the key is returned only when `tenant_id` was given; an entity not created by the plugin needs `allow_existing_id` (else `-EPERM`).
features.notes: Grants without `fsname=` apply to the same path in every file system the entity can reach. Relies on the MDS for `flock` (blocking, owner-scoped), `O_CREAT` opens and in-place rewrites of small files under `/volumes`.

features.group: Caps provisioning by the monitor and mgr
features.name: mgr/nfs export user caps
features.summary: Each CephFS NFS export gets a dedicated cephx user with an rw path grant; access type and squash are enforced by Ganesha, not by MDS caps.
features.description: mgr/nfs creates `client.nfs.<cluster>.<fs>.<sha1(cluster:fs:cmount_path)[:8]>` with `mds 'allow rw path=<cmount_path>'`, `osd 'allow rw pool=.nfs namespace=<cluster>, allow rw tag cephfs data=<fs>'`, `mon 'allow r'`, and removes it with `auth rm`. It always grants `rw` because MDS caps of an established connection do not change; the export's access type and squashing are configured in Ganesha.
features.notes: Handle-based access by Ganesha (`LOOKUPINO`) is constrained only by the mask-0 path match on the target.

features.name: Local admin socket transport
features.summary: A Unix-domain socket per daemon that accepts JSON commands from `ceph daemon`, ceph-exporter and scripts, with file-system permissions as the only access control.
features.description: Path `admin_socket`, daemon default `$run_dir/$cluster-$name.asok` (e.g. `/var/run/ceph/ceph-mds.a.asok`), mode `admin_socket_mode`; one `admin_socket` thread polls the socket. Request: a JSON command string terminated by NUL or newline, at most 1023 bytes (longer requests are logged and the connection closed without reply); a leading NUL selects the legacy binary protocol (4-byte big-endian code 0, 1, 2 = `0`, `perfcounters_dump`, `perfcounters_schema`). Reply: 4-byte big-endian length, then payload; the return code is not transmitted, a negative rc prefixes the payload with `ERROR: <strerror>\n<error string>\n`. Local requests run synchronously: the admin thread waits for asynchronous commands to finish, which blocks every other asok and tell command of the process meanwhile. `ceph daemon` fetches `get_command_descriptions` first (10 s socket timeout).
features.notes: ceph-exporter (deployed by cephadm per host and by Rook per node with `--sock-dir /run/ceph`) is the production consumer; Rook does not set `admin_socket`, so the exporter sees the C++ default path only if it resolves inside the mounted `/run/ceph` (mgr-tools page 3.9.4).

legacy_parts.note: The binary request protocol selected by a leading NUL byte: a 4-byte big-endian code 0, 1 or 2 mapped to the commands `0`, `perfcounters_dump` and `perfcounters_schema` (any other code becomes the unknown prefix `foo`). The code labels the binary form 'old protocol' since commit b389685afa1 (2012) introduced string commands. Baseline admin-socket clients send NUL-terminated JSON: the ceph CLI (ceph daemon, and Rook's ceph --admin-daemon probes) through ceph_daemon.py, and ceph-exporter through AdminSocketClient. A search of src/pybind, src/tools, src/cephadm, src/exporter and Rook found no sender of the binary form.

features.name: Remote tell transport (MCommand / MCommandReply)
features.summary: Lets `ceph tell mds.X`, mgr modules and libcephfs callers run the same command table over the messenger.
features.description: `MCommand` (type 97): `uuid fsid`, `vector<string> cmd`, data = input buffer. `MCommandReply` (98): `errorcode32_t r` (Linux errno on the wire), `string rs`, data = output, tid echoed; replies of asynchronous commands can arrive out of order. `MDSDaemon::handle_command` runs under `mds_lock`: no session on the connection -> dropped without reply (a `one_shot` caller gets `-EPIPE`); session not in the SessionMap -> connection marked disposable; caps not `allow_all()` -> `-EACCES` "permission denied"; empty cmd -> `-EINVAL` "no command given"; bad JSON -> `-EINVAL`; otherwise `queue_tell_command` hands it to the admin thread, which executes it asynchronously and sends the reply from the completing thread. Legacy `MMonCommand` ("mds tell" via monitor) is dropped with a clog warning. On a daemon without a rank every rank command returns bare `-ENOSYS` (the `{"error":"mds_not_active"}` body is discarded).

legacy_parts.note: MSG_MON_COMMAND (MMonCommand) from a monitor peer, accepted only from MON peers and discarded with the clog warning 'dropping `mds tell` command from legacy monitor'. The monitor marked `mds tell` obsolete in v12.0.2, the release in which commit 2be6297d12e replaced the MDS-side handling of relayed MMonCommand with this discard, and removed the command from MonCommands.h in v17.1.0 (commit 997208da911). Under src/mon, MMonCommand is constructed only by MonClient::_send_command (towards a monitor) and by an OSDMonitor self-dispatch, never towards an MDS. The ceph CLI, mgr modules and libcephfs reach the MDS with MCommand.
evidence_notes: git 2be6297d12e 'mds: remove legacy MMonCommand handling' (first tag v12.0.2)
git 997208da911 'mon/MonCommands: remove obsolete mds commands' (first tag v17.1.0; commit message: mds tell marked obsolete in v12.0.2)
grep of src/mon/MonCommands.h: no `mds tell` command

features.name: Tell authorization: allow * required
features.summary: Remote admin commands run only for peers whose MDS caps contain an unrestricted `*` grant; the local socket has no cephx check.
features.description: `MDSAuthCaps::allow_all()` is true when some grant has spec `*`/`all`, uid ANY (`uid=0` also counts) and an empty path (`path=/` normalizes to empty). The grant's `fsname=`, `root_squash` and `network` are not checked, so `allow * fsname=a` may run tell commands on MDS daemons of every file system and from any address. Failure gives `MCommandReply(-EACCES, "permission denied")`; the `ceph` CLI then prints "Check that your user has 'allow *' capabilities for the target daemon type". Deployed holders: cephadm gives `mgr.*` and `client.admin` `mds 'allow *'`; Rook gives the mgr `mds 'allow *'` and `client.csi-cephfs-provisioner` `mds 'allow *'` (for client eviction).

features.name: Command self-description (get_command_descriptions, help)
features.summary: Returns the signature and help of every registered command; the `ceph` CLI cannot send any MDS tell or daemon command without it.
features.description: `get_command_descriptions` returns `{"cmd000": {"sig": [<literal words>, {name, type, req?, positional?, n?, range?, strings?}], "help": "<text>"}, ...}` over all registered hooks (MDS-specific and generic), numbered in prefix order; `req` and `positional` appear only when the descriptor states them, as JSON booleans. `help` lists prefixes with non-empty help. Descriptor grammar: `<prefix words> name=<arg>,type=<CephString|CephInt|CephFloat|CephBool|CephChoices>[,req=false][,n=N][,range=min|max][,strings=a|b] ... [-- <named-only args>]`. The CLI fetches descriptions from each target before sending, splits comma-separated words for `n=N` non-positional arguments (`scrub start / recursive,repair` becomes `scrubops: [recursive, repair]`) and prints help from them (`ceph tell mds.X help`).
features.notes: MDS command registration is in `MDSDaemon::set_up_admin_socket` (60 MDS commands; 36 generic commands, 35 until `Objecter::init` adds `objecter_requests`).

features.name: Argument validation, output formats, output-file and return-code conventions
features.summary: Common parsing and output rules of every admin command, including the JSON shape quirks and the inconsistent ways commands report errors.
features.description: `execute_command`: `cmdmap_from_json` (`-EINVAL` "invalid json"), exact prefix match (`-EINVAL` "unknown command prefix"), `validate_cmd` (missing required scalar, wrong JSON type, range, choices, `CephBool` without `req=false` required; vector args never required; unknown keys ignored) -> `-EINVAL` "invalid command json". Formats: `json`, `json-pretty` (default and fallback), `xml`, `xml-pretty`, `table`, `table-kv`, `html`, `html-pretty`; the JSON formatter drops top-level section names (e.g. `cache status` is `{"pool":{...}}`, `session ls` a bare array). `output-file` writes JSON on the daemon host (only json/json-pretty, `:tmp:` uses `tmp_file_template`) and replies `{path, result, output, len}`. If `r < 0` the formatter content is discarded unless the handler flushes it itself. Conventions: rc = outcome plus `return_code` (`flush journal`, `flush_path`, `scrub abort|pause`, `quarantine`); rc always 0 with outcome only in `return_code` (`scrub start`, `tag path`, `export dir`); `scrub resume` reports 1 for failure, `qos set|rm` 1 for success; errors only in the status string (`dump tree|inode|dir`, `dirfrag *`, `qos get`); rc < 0 with JSON body (`quiesce db`, `quiesce path`, `lock path`).
features.notes: Ignoring unknown keys is relied on by mgr/volumes, which forwards its whole command dict to `quiesce db`. JSON integers become `int64_t`, so an integer literal for a `CephFloat` argument (`quiesce db --timeout`) is rejected.

features.name: Client-side target resolution for tell (libcephfs mds_command)
features.summary: The CLI and mgr resolve MDS targets against the FSMap in libcephfs; the MDS only needs correct FSMap entries.
features.description: `Client::mds_command` authenticates, fetches the latest FSMap and resolves the spec: a role `<fs name or fscid>:<rank>` or a bare rank of the legacy fs maps to the rank holder's gid (`-EAGAIN` if down); otherwise an integer is a gid (`-ENOENT` if absent), `*` means every MDS (`-ENOENT` if none), anything else a daemon name. Laggy targets are skipped (`-ENOENT` "All targeted MDS daemons are laggy" if all are). With `one_shot` the client aborts with `-EPIPE` on reset or refusal; on a mounted handle a target that becomes DNE or laggy in a later MDSMap cancels the command with `-ETIMEDOUT` "MDS <gid> went away". Multi-target successes are concatenated as `[{"mds.<name>": <out>},...]`. mgr modules use `MgrModule.send_command`/`tell_command` over a shared unmounted `LibCephFS` (`mds_command2`); the volumes evictor uses its mounted handle. `ceph tell mds.*` is expanded by the CLI from `fs dump` (standbys plus `mdsmap.info[].name`).
features.notes: Requires the MDS to appear in the FSMap with correct `addrs`, `gid`, `name`, `rank`, `state`, `laggy_since` (owned by category 01-cluster-membership-and-ha).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: status command
features.summary: Reports daemon identity, rank state, recovery progress, map epochs and system info.
features.description: `status` outputs `cluster_fsid`, `whoami` (rank or -1), `id` (gid), `want_state`, `state`, then under `mds_lock` `fs_name` and at most one of `replay_status{journal_read_pos, journal_write_pos, journal_expire_pos, num_events, num_segments}`, `resolve_status`, `reconnect_status`, `rejoin_status`, `clientreplay_status` by rank state, plus `rank_uptime`; then `mdsmap_epoch`, `osdmap_epoch`, `osdmap_epoch_barrier` (0 without a rank), `uptime`, `sysinfo{ceph_version, ..., hostname, ...}`, `endian`. It is a daemon-level command that also works without a rank.
features.notes: qa `wait_for_daemons` polls `status.state == "up:active"` (qa/tasks/cephfs/filesystem.py:1144-1154); docs use `ceph tell mds.<fs>:0 status | jq .replay_status`. Rook's generic asok `status` probe is attached to mon, mgr and OSD only, not to the MDS.

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: Process control commands: exit, respawn, lockup
features.summary: Lets operators and qa stop, re-exec or deliberately stall the daemon.
features.description: `exit` and `respawn` reply "Exiting..."/"Respawning..." in plain text; a detached thread sleeps 1 s, takes `mds_lock` and calls `suicide()` (beacon DNE, shutdown, exit) or `respawn()` (`execv` of `/proc/self/exe` with the original argv, same PID; `_exit(0)` if `mds_valgrind_exit`). The respawned process authenticates again and appears under a new gid. `lockup <ms>` sleeps in the admin thread while holding `mds_lock` (dev aid).
features.notes: qa cephtool sends `respawn` by rank and by name and waits for the rank holder gid to change (qa/workunits/cephtool/test.sh:941-957). `exit` relies on the supervisor (systemd, cephadm, Rook) to restart the process. See also F-CLU-105 (respawn).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: heap and cpu_profiler commands
features.summary: Pass-through to tcmalloc heap commands and gperftools CPU profiling; telemetry parses `heap stats`.
features.description: `heap <dump|start_profiler|stop_profiler|release|get_release_rate|set_release_rate|stats> [value]` calls `ceph_heap_profiler_handle_command`; without tcmalloc it returns `-EOPNOTSUPP` "not using tcmalloc". `cpu_profiler status|flush` drives gperftools with text in the status string. The mgr telemetry `perf_memory_metrics` collection sends `{"prefix":"heap","heapcmd":"stats"}` and expects text containing "tcmalloc heap stats" with exactly 12 integers; failures are only logged.

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: Op tracker dumps (ops, dump_ops_in_flight, blocked and historic ops)
features.summary: Lists in-flight, blocked and recently completed MDS requests with their event timelines.
features.description: All MDS requests (client, peer and internal) are `TrackedOp`s in `MDSRank::op_tracker`. `dump_ops_in_flight` -> `{ops[], num_ops}`; `dump_blocked_ops` (older than `mds_op_complaint_time`) -> `{ops[], complaint_time, num_blocked_ops}`; `dump_blocked_ops_count`; `dump_historic_ops` and `_by_duration` -> `{size, duration, ops[]}`; they run without `mds_lock`. Each op: `description`, `initiated_at`, `age`, `duration`, `continuous`, `type_data{result, flag_point, reqid, op_type, ..., events[], locks}`. `ops [--flags=locks] [--path=<file>]` takes `mds_lock` to fill `locks[]` or writes compact JSON to a file on the MDS host. With `mds_enable_op_tracker=false` they return only "op_tracker disabled; set mds_enable_op_tracker=true to enable" with rc 0.
features.notes: qa `TestValidTell` requires valid JSON from these commands (qa/tasks/cephfs/test_admin.py:306-340); docs prescribe `ceph daemon mds.<name> dump_ops_in_flight`. See also F-STORE-107 (journal op events).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: op get and op kill
features.summary: Look up or kill a single request by request id; `op kill` is the release mechanism of `lock path` and `quiesce path` ops.
features.description: `op get [--flags=locks] <reqid>` and `op kill <reqid>` parse `<entity>.<num>:<tid>` (`-EINVAL` "malformed id"), take `mds_lock` and return `-ENOENT` "request does not exist" if absent. `op kill` dumps `{result:0, request}` and calls `MDCache::request_kill`: a request with peer witnesses or waiting on peers (other than LOCK_PATH) is not killed; it is marked aborted only if it has not yet acquired all its locks, otherwise left running. Both look requests up in `MDCache` and keep working when the op tracker is disabled.
features.notes: See also F-NS-007 (request_kill semantics).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: session ls / client ls
features.summary: Dumps the client sessions of a rank; mgr/stats and the dashboard parse its output.
features.description: `session ls|client ls [--cap_dump] [filters...]` (under `mds_lock`) returns an array of `Session::dump`: `id`, `auth_name{type,type_str,id}`, `entity{name{type,num},addr{type,addr,nonce}}`, `state`, `num_leases`, `num_caps`, `caps[]` (only with cap_dump), `request_load_avg`, `uptime`, `requests_in_flight`, `num_completed_requests`, `num_completed_flushes`, `reconnecting`, recall and liveness decay counters, `delegated_inos[]`, then `inst`, `completed_requests[]`, `prealloc_inos[]` and `client_metadata{client_features{feature_bits}, metric_spec{metric_flags{feature_bits}}, <every metadata key as string>}`. `feature_bits` is `0x` plus 16 hex digits per 64-bit word, most significant first, or `0x0`. Filters as for `session evict`; only `client.*` sessions are listed.
features.notes: mgr/stats sends `client ls` to every daemon with `rank == 0` and indexes `id`, `client_metadata.hostname`, `.root` and `metric_spec.metric_flags.feature_bits` without defaults (a missing key aborts processing of that reply); the dashboard sends `session ls` to `<fscid>:0` and classifies a client as userspace by `ceph_version` and as kernel by `kernel_version`. The MDS passes through the metadata the client sent at session open (kclient: `hostname`, `kernel_version`, `entity_id`, `root`).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: session evict / client evict / session kill and the session filter grammar
features.summary: Evicts (and by default blocklists) client sessions selected by filters; used by mgr/volumes, the dashboard, operators and qa.
features.description: Filters: bare `<n>` (session id; stops parsing; bare `0` means any), `id=<n>` (`id=0` invalid, 32-bit `std::stoi` pre-check; `id=*` stops parsing), `auth_name=<id>` (cephx id without type), `state=<closed|opening|open|closing|stale|killing>`, `reconnecting=true|false|1|0`, `client_metadata.<key>=<value>` (exact match); all present criteria must match. `-EAGAIN` "MDS is replaying log" in replay or standby-replay; bad filter `-EINVAL`; no match rc 0 "no hosts match". Each matched session goes through `evict_client(wait=false, blocklist=mds_session_blocklist_on_evict)`: mon command `{"prefix":"osd blocklist","blocklistop":"add","addr":<addr>}` (result ignored), wait for the latest OSDMap, `set_osd_epoch_barrier`, then journal the kill; clog info "Evicting (and blocklisting) client session <id> (<addr>)"; the reply is sent when all kills complete. `session kill <client_id>` does the same for one session with `wait=true`, blocking the admin thread (without `mds_lock`) for the blocklist round trip and journaled kill; `-ENOENT` if unknown or replaying.
features.notes: An empty filter list (possible via raw JSON or libcephfs, since vector args are never required), `id=*` first, or bare `0` evicts every client of the rank; the CLI requires at least one word. `doc/cephfs/eviction.rst:89` shows `client_metadata.=4305`, which the parser rejects. Session teardown semantics belong to category 02-client-sessions-and-protocol.

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: session config / client config timeout
features.summary: Sets or clears the per-session `timeout` client-metadata key that changes stale-session handling.
features.description: `session config|client config <client_id> <option> [<value>]` accepts only `timeout`; with a value (checked with `strtoul(value, &end, 0)`, so hex, octal, a leading `-` and the empty string pass; stored as given) it sets `client_metadata["timeout"]`, without a value it removes it (`-ENODATA` if absent); unknown session `-ENOENT`; other options `-EINVAL`. The key makes `find_idle_sessions` never mark the session stale (0) or evict it directly once its renew age exceeds the value; `session_autoclose` still applies first. At reconnect, sessions with the key are kept for reclaim instead of being evicted. The session is not marked dirty, and the setting is per rank. Clients set the same key themselves (`ceph_set_session_timeout`; NFS-Ganesha uses 300 s before `ceph_start_reclaim`).
features.notes: See also F-PROTO-046 (semantics of the timeout key), F-CLU-096 (reclaim gating).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: flush journal
features.summary: Command-plane view of flush journal.
features.description: See F-STORE-020. Command-plane facts: registered for the admin socket and tell; the reply is `{message, return_code}` with rc = `return_code`.
features.notes: Documented operator step before offline repair. Journal mechanics belong to category 06-journal-and-storage.

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: flush_path
features.summary: Writes one inode and its parent dirfrag back to RADOS.
features.description: `flush_path <path>` starts internal op `CEPH_MDS_OP_FLUSH` (0x1502): `rdlock_path_pin_ref(want_auth=true)`, then `CInode::flush` stores the backtrace if the parent pointer is dirty and commits the parent dirfrag (or stores a base inode) if the inode is dirty. `-EROFS` on a read-only rank; internal requests are not forwarded, so on a rank that is not auth for the inode the op completes `-EXDEV`. Output `{message, return_code}`.
features.notes: Used by qa (test_scrub_checks.py:263-289).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: force_readonly
features.summary: Puts the rank into read-only mode until restart and tells clients to drop write caps.
features.description: `force_readonly` (under `mds_lock`) sets the cache read-only flag, clog-warns "force file system read-only", sends `MClientSession(CEPH_SESSION_FORCE_RO)` to every open or stale session, re-evaluates the cap locks of every head inode (revoking write caps) and flushes the log. There is no command to undo it. The same path runs automatically on an unhandled metadata write error when `mds_action_on_write_error == 1` (default). Health `MDS_READ_ONLY` is then reported. The kclient sets `s_readonly` and fails cap acquisition needing `Fw`/`Fx` with `-EROFS`; libcephfs calls `force_session_readonly`.
features.notes: See also F-PROTO-038 (FORCE_RO message), F-STORE-100 (write-error policy).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: osdmap barrier
features.summary: Sets the rank's OSD epoch barrier and waits until the Objecter has that OSDMap.
features.description: `osdmap barrier <target_epoch>` assigns `osd_epoch_barrier = target_epoch` under `mds_lock` (a plain assignment, so it can lower the barrier), then blocks the admin thread without `mds_lock` until `objecter->wait_for_map` reports the epoch. The barrier is sent to clients in cap messages.
features.notes: Only qa uses it (consumer class Q). The barrier mechanism belongs to category 06-journal-and-storage. See also F-STORE-098 (OSD epoch barrier).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: cache drop
features.summary: Recalls caps from all clients, flushes the journal and trims the cache as far as possible.
features.description: `cache drop [timeout]` repeats `Server::recall_client_state(STEADY|TRIM)`, which sends `CEPH_SESSION_RECALL_STATE` with a new `max_caps` and `CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG` to sessions above their new limit and gathers `FLUSHMSG_ACK`s, re-arming every 1 s while recall is throttled or progressing and the timeout is not exceeded; then `C_Flush_Journal`, then `trim(UINT64_MAX)` repeated while throttled. Output `client_recall{return_code, message, recalled}` (`-ETIMEDOUT` if the timeout expired; the command continues), `flush_journal{return_code, message}`, `trim_cache{trimmed}`, `cache{pool{items,bytes}}`, `duration`. `timeout = 0` (default) waits for every client.
features.notes: If the journal flush fails (e.g. `-EROFS` after `force_readonly`), `cmd_err` closes the formatter section and `C_Drop_Cache::finish` closes it again, tripping `ceph_assert` in `JSONFormatter::close_section`: the daemon aborts (inferred from code, not observed). Through the local asok an unresponsive client blocks the admin thread indefinitely. See also F-STORE-020 (journal flush state machine), F-CAPS-032 (recall).

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: cache status and dump cache
features.summary: Reports cache memory use and dumps the whole cache as JSON or to a text file on the MDS host.
features.description: `cache status` -> `{pool:{items, bytes}}` of the `mds_co` mempool. `dump cache [path] [timeout]` holds `mds_lock` for the whole dump: with `path`, a text dump (one line per inode, dirfrag and dentry) to a file opened `O_EXCL` mode 0600 relative to the daemon's working directory (empty path becomes `cachedump.<epoch>.mds<rank>`); without, a JSON array of inode dumps. Refused above `mds_dump_cache_threshold_formatter` (1 GiB; JSON `{"error":"cache usage exceeds dump threshold"}`, rc 0) or `mds_dump_cache_threshold_file` (0 = unlimited; `-EINVAL`). The timeout becomes `mds_beacon_interval/2` when <= 0 and is capped at `mds_beacon_interval`.
features.notes: A file that cannot be created returns a positive errno (e.g. 17); a file-mode timeout reports success. The dump stalls all request processing on the rank for its duration.

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: Cache and table dumps: dump tree, dump inode, dump dir, openfiles ls, dump snaps
features.summary: Debug and qa dumps of cached inodes, dirfrags and open files in C++ object formats.
features.description: `dump tree <root> [depth] [path]`: post-order array of inode dumps from a cached path (`~mdsdir`, `~mds<rank>` accepted) or a file plus `{path}`. `dump inode <number>`: one inode dump with `path`. `dump dir <path> [dentry_dump]`: per leaf fragment a `CDir` dump or `{frag, status:"dirfrag not in cache"}`. `openfiles ls`: inodes on log segments' `open_files` lists. `dump snaps` outputs the SnapClient view `{last_created, last_destroyed, snaps[]}` (`-EINVAL` if not synced), or with `--server` the SnapServer table (`-EXDEV` "Not snapserver" on other ranks). Path arguments are resolved with `cache_traverse`, which never loads from RADOS; misses are reported in the status string with rc 0.
features.notes: qa `test_volumes.py` reads `old_inodes` counts from `dump inode` output (`_verify_old_inodes`, test_volumes.py:498-560), which ties that test to the C++ inode dump format. `dump snaps --server` lists last_snap, last_created, last_destroyed, pending_noop, snaps, need_to_purge, pending_update and pending_destroy (not the version); `openfiles ls` lists the segments' open_files lists, not the OpenFileTable, so on an active rank it shows almost nothing about ordinary open files. qa/tasks/cephfs/test_snapshots.py uses `dump snaps`.

features.group: Admin commands: daemon, sessions, journal and cache
features.name: dump stray
features.summary: Command-plane view of dump stray.
features.description: See F-BG-027. Command-plane facts: `dump stray` is registered for the admin socket and tell, runs MDCache::stray_status under mds_lock, waits for frozen stray dirfrags and fetches incomplete ones before completing, and reports this rank's strays only.
features.notes: Documented in troubleshooting (`ceph tell mds.<fs>:0 dump stray`). Strays belong to category 09-background-services.

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: Scrub control commands (scrub start, abort, pause, resume, status, purge_status)
features.summary: Command-plane view of the scrub control commands; the scrub behaviour of each command is catalogued in 09-background-services.
features.description: See F-BG-028 (scrub start), F-BG-036 (scrub pause, resume, abort), F-BG-037 (scrub status and summaries) and F-BG-038 (scrub purge_status and counters). Command-plane facts: all scrub commands except `scrub status` require rank 0 (`-EXDEV` "Not rank 0") and start/abort/pause/resume also `up:active` (`-EINVAL`, checked first); they are reached through the admin socket or `ceph tell mds.<fs>:0` (tell needs `allow *`, F-ADM-028); command rc is 0 once those checks pass and errors appear in the `return_code` field; rank 0 relays pause/resume/abort to the other up ranks with `MMDSScrub`.
features.notes: Docs prescribe `ceph tell mds.<fs>:0 scrub start|status|abort|pause|resume`; qa asserts `return_code == 0`. `scrub_path` is registered but has no handler (always `-ENOSYS`); `scrub_start` has a handler but no registration (unreachable).

legacy_parts.note: `scrub_path`, still registered in MDSDaemon::set_up_admin_socket but without a handler branch, so it always returns -ENOSYS. The `scrub_start` branch of MDSRankDispatcher::handle_asok_command, which cannot run because no command is registered under that prefix and the admin socket dispatches only exact registered prefixes. Commit 8a2f2625799 (first tag v15.1.0) merged `scrub_path` and `scrub_start` into `scrub start` and left both remnants. No sender of `scrub_path` or `scrub_start` exists in src/pybind/mgr, src/tools, src/cephadm, qa/tasks or Rook; documentation and qa use `scrub start`.

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: tag path and the scrub_tag xattr
features.summary: Command-plane view of tag path.
features.description: See F-BG-030 (tag path) and F-BG-029 (scrub tags and the scrub_tag xattr). Command-plane facts: `tag path <path> <tag>` is rank-0 only and its reply follows the scrub start convention (rc 0, `return_code`).
features.notes: The scrub_tag xattr on object 0 is listed in the RADOS object catalog (F-STORE-063).

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: damage ls and damage rm
features.summary: Command-plane view of damage ls and damage rm.
features.description: See F-BG-059. Command-plane facts: both commands are registered for the admin socket and tell on every rank and act on that rank's table only; a non-empty table raises MDS_DAMAGE (F-ADM-078).
features.notes: Documented operator procedure (`ceph tell mds.<id> damage ls|rm`, damaged-rank.rst). The damage table belongs to category 09-background-services (F-BG-052).

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: Multi-MDS inspection and control: get subtrees, dump loads, export dir, dump_export_states
features.summary: Shows the subtree map and balancer loads and lets qa force a subtree export.
features.description: `get subtrees` -> array of `{is_auth, auth_first, auth_second, export_pin, distributed_ephemeral_pin, random_ephemeral_pin, export_pin_target, dir{...}}`. `dump loads [depth]` -> `dirfrags[]`, `mds_load{mds.N:{request_rate, cache_hit_rate, queue_length, cpu_load, mds_load, ...}}`, `mds_meta_load`, `mds_import_map`. `export dir <path> <rank>` checks the target rank and cached auth fragment (`-ENOENT`, `-EINVAL`), then `Migrator::export_dir`, which silently returns for pinned, frozen, stray, quiesced or quarantined directories and degraded clusters; output `{return_code}`, rc 0, completion not reported. `dump_export_states` lists exports in progress with state history.
features.notes: Consumers are qa only (class Q). Migration belongs to category 07-multi-mds.

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: dirfrag split, merge and ls
features.summary: Manual fragmentation control and listing of a directory's fragtree leaves.
features.description: `dirfrag split <path> <frag> <bits>`, `dirfrag merge <path> <frag>` (`frag` = `<hex value>/<bits>`) need a cached auth fragment and `can_fragment` (not read-only, degraded, root, mdsdir, stray, quiesced; no scrub or fragmenting; depth at most 24 bits). Argument and lookup failures appear only in the status string with rc 0; refusals inside `MDCache::split_dir`/`merge_dir` are silent. `dirfrag ls <path>` lists the leaves under `frag_t()` as `[{value, bits, str}]`, including fragments not in cache.
features.notes: Fragmentation belongs to category 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags. See also F-CACHE-086 (fragmentation preconditions).

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: lock path and quiesce path test hooks
features.summary: Test hooks that acquire named locks on an inode, or quiesce one subtree, through internal requests held until `op kill`.
features.description: `lock path <path> [locks...] [--ap-dont-block] [--ap-freeze] [--await] [--lifetime <s>]` starts internal op `CEPH_MDS_OP_LOCK_PATH` (0x150a): traversal with `DISCOVER|RDLOCK_PATH|WANT_INODE`, then each `<lock>:<kind>` with lock in `quiesce|snap|policy|file|nest|dft|auth|link|xattr|flock` and kind `r|w|x`. `--ap-dont-block` turns an auth-pin conflict into `-EAGAIN`; `--ap-freeze` freezes the inode. Once locked the op holds its locks until `op kill`; `--lifetime` only cancels an op still acquiring (`-ECANCELED`). Without `--await` the reply is the current op dump; with it, the reply comes when locks are held, the op fails or the lifetime expires. The op is `continuous`, so it never counts as a slow request. `quiesce path <path> [--await]` starts internal op `CEPH_MDS_OP_QUIESCE_PATH` (0x1508) and replies `{op, state}` (request dump and `QuiesceStatistics`), immediately or on completion with `--await`; `-EAGAIN` on a rank that is not `up:active`; it also holds its locks until `op kill`.
features.notes: `lock path` without `--await`: any failure in `dispatch_lock_path` reaches `ceph_abort_msg("trying to respond to internal op without finisher")` and aborts the daemon. `quiesce path` without `--await` that completes synchronously calls `finish()` on an already freed context (use-after-free, usually harmless). Both inferred from code, not observed. Used by qa test_quiesce.py; the quiesce mechanism belongs to category 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine. lock path details: anything outside the listed lock types and r/w/x gives -EINVAL; without --ap-freeze the auth pins are dropped after locking; once locked the op is released only by op kill or a restart (the --lifetime timer kills it with -ECANCELED only while mdr->result is unset, i.e. before the locks are held; dispatch_lock_path sets result 0 on success); request_kill ignores pending peer requests for this op type; a quiesce:x lock taken this way blocks mutations but does not mask caps (is_quiesced() is false); by code reading nest:x or dft:x reaches ceph_abort() and quiesce:r trips an assert. quiesce path runs quiesce_path on the local rank, bypassing the quiesce DB, and its state reply has {inodes, inodes_quiesced, inodes_blocked, inodes_dropped, failed: [{request, result}]}; the DB never releases this op. See also F-QOS-043 (tree quiesce request), F-CAPS-096 (lock dumps).

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: quiesce db command
features.summary: Command-plane view of quiesce db and how mgr/volumes calls it.
features.description: See F-QOS-053. Command-plane facts: `quiesce db` is registered for the admin socket and tell (tell needs `allow *`), runs without `mds_lock`, and on a non-leader returns `-ENOTTY` with body `{epoch, leader}` so that callers can retry at the leader. mgr/volumes (`fs quiesce`, F-ADM-101) sends its whole command dict (extra keys ignored) to `mdsmap.qdb_leader` with `one_shot`, retrying up to 5 times on `-ENOTTY` using `leader` from the output, and passes the output to users verbatim.
features.notes: After leadership loss before processing, the body has `epoch` and `set_version` 0 and `leader` = own gid. The quiesce protocol belongs to category 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine.

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: quarantine enable / disable command
features.summary: Command-plane view of quarantine enable and disable.
features.description: See F-QOS-058. Command-plane facts: `quarantine enable|disable <path>` is registered for the admin socket and tell (tell needs `allow *`); internal ops are not forwarded, so the command must reach the rank that is auth for the subvolume root's dentry (else `-EXDEV`).
features.notes: mgr/volumes sends it to the first `up:active`/`up:clientreplay` entry of sorted `mdsmap.up` (normally rank 0); its comment says the MDS forwards, but internal ops are not forwarded, so the call works only if that rank is auth for the `/volumes/<group>` dirfrag holding the subvolume dentry (inferred, not observed; F-ADM-102).

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: QoS commands (dump qos, qos set, qos rm, qos get)
features.summary: Command-plane view of the dmClock QoS commands.
features.description: See F-QOS-007 (qos set, qos rm) and F-QOS-008 (dump qos, qos get). Command-plane facts: the four commands are registered for the admin socket and tell (tell needs `allow *`); `qos set` and `qos rm` report success as `return_code` 1 and failure as 0 with command rc always 0; settings are in memory and per rank.
features.notes: Documented in doc/cephfs/mds-qos.rst; no mgr consumer. The scheduler belongs to category 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine.

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: Generic process commands: perf, counter, config, log, injectargs
features.summary: Commands every Ceph daemon carries; several are consumed by tooling and qa.
features.description: `perf dump [logger] [counter]`, `perf schema`, `perf histogram dump|schema`, `perf reset`, legacy `perfcounters_dump|schema`, `counter dump`, `counter schema` (registered by `CephContext`); `config show|help|set|unset|get|diff|diff get`, `injectargs` (changes reach `MDSRankDispatcher::handle_conf_change`); `log flush|dump|reopen`; debug-only `assert`, `abort`, `leak_some_memory`, `objecter_requests` (registered by `Objecter::init`, absent on a rank-less standby), `messenger dump`, `raise [signal] [cancel] [after]`. ceph-exporter uses `counter dump`, `counter schema` and `config show` (`pid_file`); qa uses `perf dump` heavily and `config`/`injectargs`.
features.notes: The `log`, `objecter_requests`, `messenger dump`, `raise`, `assert`, `abort` and `leak_some_memory` commands have no consumer for the MDS in the tree (class D on the admin-commands page); log rotation uses SIGHUP.

legacy_parts.note: Hidden aliases `perfcounters_dump` and `1` (for `perf dump`) and `perfcounters_schema` and `2` (for `perf schema`), also reached through the binary admin-socket codes 1 and 2. Commit ca8f3ba8e9e (2012) renamed these commands to `perf dump` and `perf schema` and left the old names registered with empty help, which hides them from `help`. ceph-exporter sends `counter dump` and `counter schema`, `ceph daemonperf` sends `perf schema` and `perf dump`, and a search of src/pybind, src/tools, src/cephadm, src/exporter and Rook found no sender of the old names (the only other mentions are crimson's OSD admin hooks and doc/radosgw).

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: dump_mempools
features.summary: Dumps per-mempool item and byte counts; telemetry collects it.
features.description: `dump_mempools` (registered by the `MempoolObs`) outputs `{mempool{by_pool{<pool>{items, bytes}}, total}}`. mgr telemetry (`perf_memory_metrics` collection) sends it with `format=json` to every MDS in `mds_metadata` and reads `mempool.by_pool.<pool>.{bytes,items}`.

features.group: Admin commands: scrub, damage, multi-MDS, quiesce, quarantine, QoS
features.name: Version and ping built-ins (0, version, git_version)
features.summary: Minimal admin socket commands used for liveness and version checks.
features.description: `0` returns raw `2` (`CEPH_ADMIN_SOCK_VERSION`); ceph-exporter sends `{"prefix":"0"}` as a ping and expects a 1-byte reply, reporting `ceph_daemon_socket_up 0` when it fails. `version` -> `{version, release, release_type}`, `git_version` -> `{git_version}`.
