features.name: MDS option catalogue and option metadata
features.summary: Declares the 201 MDS options with type, level, default, limits and flags; names and semantics are read by operators, docs, orchestrators and mgr modules.
features.description: `src/common/options/mds.yaml.in` declares 201 options (199 `mds_*` plus `defer_client_eviction_on_laggy_osds` and `subv_metrics_window_interval`): 2 `basic` (`mds_join_fs`, `mds_cache_memory_limit`), 131 `advanced`, 68 `dev`; 89 `runtime`, 3 `startup`, 1 `no_mon_update` (`mds_data`). Types are `bool`, `int`, `uint`, `float`, `size`, `secs`, `millisecs`, `str`. `Option::can_update_at_runtime()` is true for `runtime` options and for every numeric/bool option not flagged `startup`, `cluster_create` or `create`, so 197 of 201 can change at runtime (the exceptions are `mds_data` and the three `startup` options, refused with `-EPERM`). `with_legacy: true` (75 options) generates lock-free `g_conf()->mds_xxx` fields. The monitor validates `ceph config set` against its own compiled option table, so a new option name can be stored only with `--force` as an untyped stray string.
features.notes: Each option is assigned to its owning category in the catalog where one exists (cache, sessions, journal, balancer, purge/scrub, QoS, ...); the per-option table with apply class is on the config page section 5.1. Options declared elsewhere also govern the MDS: `osd_op_complaint_time`, `osd_max_write_size`, `osd_deep_scrub_large_omap_object_key_threshold`, `osd_num_op_tracker_shard`, `perf`. `mds_beacon_grace`, `mds_beacon_interval` and `mds_enforce_unique_name` are also evaluated by the monitor with its own copy. Five options lack `services: [mds]`.

features.name: Runtime config observer and per-subsystem fan-out
features.summary: Delivers changed option values to the rank and its subsystems; only tracked keys reach the MDS code.
features.description: `MDSRankDispatcher` is the single observer; `get_tracked_keys()` returns a static sorted list of 96 keys (85 real MDS options, 2 misspelled names, 7 `clog_*`, `fsid`, `host`). `ConfigProxy::_gather_changes` delivers only tracked changed keys; an untracked key is reported as "(not observed, change may require restart)". `handle_conf_change` runs on the delivering thread without `mds_lock`, applies heartbeat graces, op-tracker settings, the in-memory log dump, clog settings and one injection option inline, then queues a lambda on the `mds-rank-fin` finisher that takes `mds_lock` and calls the `handle_conf_change` of SessionMap, Server, MDCache (-> Migrator, MDBalancer), MDLog, PurgeQueue, ScrubStack and the dmClock scheduler in that order. Registration does not replay values; a rank-less standby has no observer; every option is re-read when the rank object is built.
features.notes: Live reads through `g_conf().get_val<T>()` take the process-wide `ConfigProxy::lock` and a string lookup on hot paths (`CDir::fetch`, `Server::recall_client_state`, `Beacon::_send`, `MDCache::upkeep_main`, `notify_health`). See also F-QOS-006 (dmClock defaults).

features.name: Config delivery from the monitor config DB and reporting to the mgr
features.summary: Options come from ceph.conf, the mon config DB (`MConfig`) or `config set` commands; the running configuration is reported to the mgr for `ceph config show`.
features.description: At startup `ceph.conf` and the mon config DB are applied in `global_init` before any MDS object exists; later `MConfig` messages (every option of the sections `global`, `mds`, `mds.<id>` as strings) are applied on the MonClient finish strand via `set_mon_vals`; `ceph tell|daemon mds.X config set` is applied on the admin thread. Values for unknown options are skipped; values for `no_mon_update` options or ones `_set_val` rejects are recorded as ignored mon values. The daemon sends its running configuration, ignored mon values and defaults in `MMgrOpen.config_bl`/`config_defaults_bl` and again in `MMgrReport.config_bl` when it changed; the mgr serves `ceph config show[-with-defaults] mds.<id>` from that copy.
features.notes: The monitor renames stored legacy names `mds_session_blacklist_on_timeout`/`_on_evict` to the `blocklist` spelling at load (src/mon/ConfigMonitor.cc:777-786). Rook writes per-daemon `mds_join_fs`/`mds_cache_memory_limit` and arbitrary user options (`config assimilate-conf`, `rook-config-override` ConfigMap) through this path.

legacy_parts.note: ConfigMonitor::load_config renaming stored `mds_session_blacklist_on_timeout` and `mds_session_blacklist_on_evict` (and five other pre-Pacific `blacklist` option names) to the `blocklist` spelling. The rename covers config-DB keys written by monitors before Pacific; when min_mon_release is pacific or later the monitor also schedules a cleanup that stores them under the new names, so current monitors convert them at their first load. No baseline peer writes the old names: in src/pybind/mgr, src/cephadm and Rook the word appears only in comments of mgr/mirroring. The MDS receives only the `blocklist` names in MConfig.

features.name: Option apply-class anomalies
features.summary: Documents options whose runtime changes are silently ignored, whose configured initial value is ignored, or that are never read.
features.description: Class X (handler exists but key not tracked or misspelled; runtime change ignored): `mds_cap_acquisition_throttle_retry_request_timeout` (tracked as `..._request_time`), `mds_log_minor_segments_per_major_segment` (tracked as `mds_log_major_segment_event_ratio`), `mds_fscrypt_last_block_max_size`, `mds_client_delegate_inos_pct`, `mds_log_warn_factor`, `mds_op_history_slow_op_size`, `mds_op_history_slow_op_threshold`, `mds_scrub_stats_review_period`. Class I (initial value hard-coded, only a later runtime change applies): `mds_allow_async_dirops` (`Server.h:618` starts `true`), `mds_extraordinary_events_dump_interval` (starts 0). Class U (never read): `mds_asio_thread_count` (pool hard-coded to 2), `mds_debug_auth_pins`, `mds_kill_journal_at`. Class S (read once): e.g. `mds_beacon_interval` (per process), `mds_decay_halflife`, `mds_dir_max_commit_size`, `mds_log_segment_size`, `subv_metrics_window_interval`.
features.notes: Crash-prone values found by code inspection (not tested), none guarded by `min`/`max`: `mds_client_delegate_inos_pct > 100` divides by zero (src/mds/Server.cc:2603-2605), `mds_heartbeat_reset_grace = 0` is a modulo by zero (src/mds/CDir.cc:2177), `mds_bal_mode` outside {0,1,2} hits `ceph_abort()`. Misleading units: `mds_heartbeat_reset_grace` is an iteration count, `mds_sleep_rank_change` microseconds, `mds_scrub_stats_review_period` days.

legacy_parts.note: Class U options that no code reads: mds_asio_thread_count (main hard-codes io_context_pool ctxpool(2)), mds_debug_auth_pins and mds_kill_journal_at. No reference to these three names exists in src (C++ and Python) or qa outside src/common/options/mds.yaml.in, so setting them has no effect, and no mgr module, cephadm or Rook sets them. They are remnants of removed code: the mds_asio_thread_count reader added by commit 73f5249f3f1 was reverted by 54ddf2c8973 (2019), the last mds_debug_auth_pins reader was removed by 6de9090502a (2018), and mds_kill_journal_at was removed from config_opts.h as unused by 1c11d31c342 (2017) but is still declared.
evidence_notes: grep of src (*.cc, *.h, *.py, *.yaml) and qa: no reference outside mds.yaml.in

features.name: MDS option names read or written by peers
features.summary: A few MDS option names are part of the contract with orchestrators, mgr modules and ceph-fuse.
features.description: cephadm runs `config set mds.<service_id> mds_join_fs <service_id>` for each MDS service (removed with `config rm` on purge) and, when autotuning OSD memory, subtracts each MDS daemon's `mds_cache_memory_limit` from host memory. Rook sets `mds_join_fs=<fs>` and `mds_cache_memory_limit` (pod memory limit x 0.5, or request x 0.8) per daemon on every reconcile. snap_schedule reads `mds_max_snaps_per_dir` with `get_foreign_ceph_option('mds', ...)` and keeps at most that value minus 1 scheduled snapshots. ceph-fuse without faked inode numbers assumes the 4096 cap of `mds_max_snaps_per_dir` in its 16-bit snapshot "stag" space and aborts with "run out of stag" beyond ~65533 referenced snapshots of one inode.
features.notes: `mds_join_fs` is sent in every beacon and resolved by the monitor to standby affinity (owned by category 01-cluster-membership-and-ha).

features.name: Fault injection, killpoints and debug options
features.summary: Dev-level options used by qa to inject failures, crash at numbered points or add expensive checks.
features.description: Killpoints `mds_kill_mdstable_at`, `_export_at`, `_import_at`, `_link_at`, `_rename_at`, `_openc_at`, `_create_at`, `_dirfrag_at`, `_shutdown_at`, `_journal_expire_at`, `_journal_replay_at` are numbered `ceph_assert(value != N)` checks; `mds_kill_after_journal_logs_flushed` dies right after a create-type event is safe. Injection: `mds_inject_health_dummy` (adds an `MDS_HEALTH_DUMMY` ERR metric the monitor stores but does not turn into a check), `mds_inject_traceless_reply_probability`, `mds_inject_rename_corrupt_dentry_first`, `mds_inject_journal_corrupt_dentry_first`, `mds_inject_migrator_session_race`, `mds_inject_skip_replaying_inotable`, `mds_server_dispatch_killpoint_random`, `mds_server_dispatch_client_request_delay`, `mds_thrash_exports`, `mds_thrash_fragments`. Debug checks: `mds_verify_scatter`, `mds_debug_scatterstat`, `mds_debug_frag`, `mds_debug_subtrees`, `mds_dump_cache_on_map`, `mds_dump_cache_after_rejoin`, `mds_shutdown_check`, `mds_connect_bootstrapping`, `mds_sleep_rank_change`.
features.notes: qa suites set these by name; a re-implementation without them cannot run those qa jobs unchanged (14-testing map page). See also F-NS-009 (request path), F-STORE-112 (journal and tables).

features.name: Unlabeled MDS perf counter loggers
features.summary: Eight loggers with 181 counters (`mds`, `mds_mem`, `mds_server`, `mds_cache`, `mds_log`, `mds_sessions`, `purge_queue`, `oft`) describing requests, caps, cache, journal, sessions and purge.
features.description: Counts: `mds` 57, `mds_mem` 14, `mds_server` 42 (including 32 `req_<op>_latency` averages), `mds_cache` 29, `mds_log` 19, `mds_sessions` 9, `purge_queue` 7, `oft` 4. They are built in `MDSRank::create_logger` and the subsystem builders while the daemon holds a rank; a rank-less standby exposes no MDS loggers. Types: gauge (`add_u64`), counter (`add_u64_counter`), time average (`add_time_avg`: sum, count, avgtime), with nick, description, unit and priority (CRITICAL 10, INTERESTING 8, USEFUL 5, UNINTERESTING 2, DEBUGONLY 0). Updates are lock-free atomics and no-ops when the global option `perf` is false. Index numbers are process-local; only names, types, priorities, nicks, descriptions and units are visible.
features.notes: Semantic traps: `mds.inodes` counts LRU dentries; `reply_latency` and `req_*_latency` stop at the early reply; `mds.request` includes replayed and dropped requests; `mds_mem.rss` is KiB but `mds_mem.heap` bytes; several counters declared as gauges are incremented (`mds.inodes_expired`, `mds.scrub_*`, `mds_log.evlrg`, `mds_sessions.mdthresh_evicted`, `oft.omap_total_updates/removes`); `ceph_cap_op_flushsnap_ack`/`flush_ack` descriptions are copy-pasted; `dir_update` and other replication counters are DEBUGONLY because they are declared before `set_prio_default`. Functional use: `MDBalancer::get_load` reads `mds.request`, `mds.traverse` and `mds.traverse_hit` back to derive `req_rate` and `cache_hit_rate` (src/mds/MDBalancer.cc:361-387), so `perf=false` keeps both at 0 and `perf reset` zeroes them for one interval (category 07-multi-mds). See also F-STORE-105 (journal counters).

features.name: Counter reporting to the mgr and the names mgr modules read
features.summary: Counters with priority at or above the mgr threshold are sent in `MMgrReport`; status, dashboard, telemetry, prometheus, influx and telegraf read specific names.
features.description: `MgrClient::_send_report` declares and sends counters with `prio >= stats_threshold` every `stats_period`; both come from the mgr in `MMgrConfigure` (`mgr_stats_threshold` 5, `mgr_stats_period` 5 s, autotunable). Names read by mgr modules: `mds_mem.{ino,dn,dir,cap}`, `mds_sessions.session_count`, rate of `mds_server.handle_client_request`, `mds_log.{ev,replayed}`, `mds_cache.num_strays`, `mds.{inodes,caps,subtrees,exported_inodes,imported_inodes,root_rfiles,root_rbytes,root_rsnaps}`; influx/telegraf export every unlabeled counter with prio >= 5. `ceph daemonperf mds.X` shows counters with prio >= 8 by nick from `perf schema`/`perf dump`.
features.notes: The dashboard also reads `mds.exported`/`mds.imported` (DEBUGONLY, never sent by default) and `mds_log.replay` (no such counter), so those series are empty (stale consumer in the tree). See also F-PROTO-104 (MgrClient).

features.name: Labeled perf counter families (client, subvolume and rank metrics)
features.summary: Dynamically created labeled counters on rank 0 (and per rank for `mds_rank_perf`) exported through `counter dump` and ceph-exporter.
features.description: Families: `mds_client_metrics` {fs_name, id} with `num_clients`; `mds_client_metrics-<fs_name>` {client, rank} with `cap_hits`, `cap_miss`, `avg_read_latency`, `avg_write_latency`, `avg_metadata_latency`, `dentry_lease_hits|miss`, `opened_files`, `opened_inodes`, `pinned_icaps`, `total_inodes`, `total_read_ops|size`, `total_write_ops|size`; `mds_subvolume_metrics` {subvolume_path, fs_name} with `avg_read_iops`, `avg_read_tp_Bps`, `avg_read_lat_msec`, `avg_write_*`, `quota_bytes`, `used_bytes`; `mds_rank_perf` {rank} with `cpu_usage`, `open_requests`. They appear in `counter dump`/`counter schema` only, not in `perf dump`; the per-client family name embeds the fs name, so its Prometheus names do too (e.g. `ceph_mds_client_metrics_cephfs_cap_hits`).
features.notes: Metric semantics belong to category 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine. The shipped Grafana subvolume dashboard queries `ceph_mds_subvolume_metrics_*` and the CephFS dashboard `ceph_mds_rank_perf_cpu_usage`/`open_requests`. See also F-QOS-024, F-QOS-025, F-QOS-022 (when the families are created and updated).

features.name: Admin-socket counter dump and schema JSON format
features.summary: The JSON shape of `perf dump|schema` and `counter dump|schema` that ceph-exporter and qa parse.
features.description: Schema entries carry `type` (bitmask: TIME 1, U64 2, LONGRUNAVG 4, COUNTER 8), `metric_type` (`counter` if COUNTER else `gauge`), `value_type` (`integer`, `real`, `integer-integer-pair`, `real-integer-pair`, histogram types), `description`, `nick`, `priority`, `units` (`none`|`bytes`). A time average value is `{avgcount, sum[, max_inc], avgtime}` with `sum`/`avgtime` printed as `<sec>.<nanosec>`; a u64 average is `{sum, avgcount[, max_inc]}`. Labeled counters appear as an array under the family name of `{labels:{...}, counters:{...}}`. `perf dump`/`perf schema` cover unlabeled loggers only.

features.name: Prometheus export through ceph-exporter
features.summary: ceph-exporter scrapes each daemon's admin socket and turns counters into Prometheus metrics; dashboards and alerts key on the resulting names and labels.
features.description: ceph-exporter scans `*.asok` in `exporter_sock_dir` (default `/var/run/ceph/`; Rook `--sock-dir /run/ceph`), pings with `{"prefix":"0"}`, reads `counter dump`, `counter schema` (counters with `priority >= exporter_prio_limit`, default 5) and `config show` (`pid_file`, for process metrics). Names are `ceph_<logger>_<counter>` with `.`, `/`, space and `-` mapped to `_`, trailing `-` to `_minus` and `+` to `_plus` (`mds_mem.ino+` -> `ceph_mds_mem_ino_plus`); a LONGRUNAVG counter becomes `<name>_count` and `<name>_sum`. Labels are the counter labels plus `ceph_daemon` = socket name without `ceph-` and `.asok` (`mds.<id>`), which dashboards join with `ceph_mds_metadata`. An empty or unparsable reply only skips that daemon for the scrape.
features.notes: Daemon-name quirks: sockets whose name contains `mgr` or `ceph-exporter` are skipped (an MDS id containing "mgr" is never scraped); a name containing `rgw` is treated as an RGW instance (`instance_id` label instead of `ceph_daemon`; with fewer than four dot-separated parts every counter is dropped). The mgr `prometheus` module no longer exports perf counters by default (`exclude_perf_counters=True`).

features.name: Memory gauges and gauge refresh cadence
features.summary: Process memory and object-count gauges and the points at which cache gauges are refreshed.
features.description: `mds_mem.rss` (KiB, `VmRSS`) and `mds_mem.heap` (bytes of anonymous rw mappings, `[heap]` and `[stack]`) are sampled by `MDCache::check_memory_usage` every `mds_cache_trim_interval` (1 s) in the upkeep thread under `mds_lock`; `mds_mem.{ino,dir,dn,cap}` and the `+`/`-` lifetime counters are copied by `update_mlogger` after each message dispatched at depth 1 while not laggy. `MDCache::log_stat` refreshes `mds.inodes`, `inodes_pinned`, `inodes_with_caps`, `caps`, LRU segment gauges and `root_r*` every tick (`mds_tick_interval` 5 s, skipped while laggy) and at the end of every request; `mds.load_cent` and `mds.q` change only with balancer heartbeats; session, log, purge and stray gauges are event-driven; `oft.*` on each open-file-table commit.
features.notes: The shipped Grafana "Memory" panel plots heap and rss with unit `kbytes`, so heap is shown 1024 times too large.

features.name: Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alerts shipped with Ceph
features.summary: The monitoring mixin queries MDS metric names and health check codes; these define which names dashboards and alerts expect.
features.description: The shipped `cephfsdashboard.json` queries `ceph_mds_server_handle_client_request`, `ceph_mds_sessions_session_count`, `ceph_mds_inodes`, `ceph_mds_forward`, `ceph_mds_reply_latency_sum|_count`, `ceph_mds_caps`, `ceph_mds_server_handle_peer_request`, `ceph_mds_log_evadd|ev|seg`, `ceph_mds_mem_ino|dn|heap|rss`, `ceph_mds_exported_inodes`, `ceph_mds_imported_inodes`, `ceph_objecter_op_r|op_w`, `ceph_mds_rank_perf_cpu_usage|open_requests`, joined `on(ceph_daemon)` with `ceph_mds_metadata` and `on(fs_id)` with `ceph_fs_metadata`; other dashboards use `ceph_mds_metadata` and `ceph_mds_subvolume_metrics_*`. Alerts key on `ceph_health_detail` codes `MDS_DAMAGE`, `MDS_ALL_DOWN`, `FS_DEGRADED`, `MDS_UP_LESS_THAN_MAX`, `MDS_INSUFFICIENT_STANDBY`, `FS_WITH_FAILED_MDS` and `MDS_HEALTH_READ_ONLY`; none keys on the per-MDS warnings (`MDS_TRIM`, `MDS_SLOW_REQUEST`, ...).
features.notes: The `CephFilesystemReadOnly` alert matches `MDS_HEALTH_READ_ONLY` but the emitted code is `MDS_READ_ONLY`, so it never fires (prometheus_alerts.yml:333). The jsonnet source still queries `ceph_mds_server_handle_slave_request` and is out of sync with the shipped JSON.

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: Health metric pipeline (MDSHealth in beacons to monitor checks)
features.summary: Each active rank recomputes a list of health metrics every tick and ships it in its beacon; the monitor turns them into cluster health checks.
features.description: `Beacon::notify_health` runs under `mds_lock` at the end of every non-laggy tick (and in `damaged()`), clears and rebuilds `health.metrics` in a fixed order; the `mds-beacon` thread copies the snapshot into each `MMDSBeacon`. Wire: `MDSHealth{vector<MDSHealthMetric>}` and `MDSHealthMetric{u16 type (!= 0), u8 sev (ERR 0, WARN 1, OK 2), string message, map<string,string> metadata}`, both `ENCODE_START(1,1)`, after `compat` in the beacon payload; ids `TRIM=1 ... DUMMY=17`. The monitor compares `type`, `sev` and `message` element-wise; any difference goes to `prepare_beacon`, which logs cleared types ("MDS health message cleared (mds.X): <old message>"), stores the metrics under `mds_health/<gid>` and bumps the MDSMap epoch. `encode_pending` makes checks with code `mds_metric_name(type)`, summary `mds_metric_summary(type)` and detail lines `mds.<name>(mds.<rank>): <message>` followed by the metric metadata as ` key: value, key: value` (src/mon/MDSMonitor.cc:310-321); unknown ids give code `???`. Per-client metrics above `mds_health_summarize_threshold` (10) are collapsed into `_MANY` metrics.
features.notes: A metric with type 0 aborts the decoding monitor (`ceph_assert`). Every distinct health vector costs a monitor proposal and a new MDSMap epoch pushed to all subscribers including mounted clients; messages that embed changing numbers (TRIM count, SLOW_REQUEST count, CACHE_OVERSIZED bytes, SLOW_METADATA_IO age, ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME) change the vector on many ticks. A laggy tick returns early, so beacons keep the last snapshot; standbys report none. The beacon itself belongs to category 01-cluster-membership-and-ha. See also F-CLU-028 (beacon side), F-CLU-021 (beacon message).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: MDS_TRIM: behind on trimming
features.summary: Warns when the journal holds more segments than the trim target allows.
features.description: Metric `TRIM` (1), check `MDS_TRIM`, HEALTH_WARN, when `segments.size() > mds_log_max_segments * mds_log_warn_factor` (default > 256); message "Behind on trimming (N/M)" with metadata `num_segments`, `max_segments`; summary "%num% MDSs behind on trimming". The monitor refuses `mds fail` and `fs fail` targeting a daemon that reports it unless `--yes-i-really-mean-it` is given.
features.notes: The segment count includes expiring and expired-but-untrimmed segments. Runtime changes of mds_log_warn_factor do not reach MDLog (not a tracked key). See also F-STORE-018 (trimming), F-ADM-083 (health-gated commands).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: Client-behaviour warnings: late cap release, cache-pressure recall, oldest tid
features.summary: Names clients that fail to release caps, respond to recall or advance their oldest request/flush tid.
features.description: `MDS_CLIENT_LATE_RELEASE` (3, `_MANY` 5): a client's oldest revoking cap is older than the MDSMap `session_timeout` (60 s), "Client H failing to respond to capability release". `MDS_CLIENT_RECALL` (2, `_MANY` 4): decayed `recall_caps` > `mds_recall_warning_threshold` (256 Ki) and `num_caps` > `mds_min_caps_working_set` (10000), "Client H failing to respond to cache pressure". `MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID` (6, `_MANY` 7): completed requests or flushes >= `mds_max_completed_requests|flushes` (100000) with trim warnings pending, "Client H failing to advance its oldest client/flush tid. ". All WARN with metadata `client_id`, or `client_count` for the `_MANY` forms ("Many clients (N) ...") above `mds_health_summarize_threshold`. Matching clog warnings: `client.N isn't responding to mclientcaps(revoke), ...`, `client.N does not advance its oldest_client_tid|oldest_flush_tid ...`.
features.notes: qa tests (e.g. qa/tasks/cephfs/test_client_limits.py) and log ignorelists match these codes and texts; client test hooks `client_inject_release_failure` and `client_inject_fixed_oldest_tid` provoke them. See also F-CAPS-032 (recall), F-CAPS-031 (late revocation).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: MDS_SLOW_REQUEST and slow-request detection
features.summary: Counts requests older than the complaint time and logs them to the cluster log with exponential backoff.
features.description: Requests are `TrackedOp`s whose age counts from message receipt (dispatch-queue and throttle time included). On every non-laggy tick `check_ops_in_flight` asks the tracker for ops older than `mds_op_complaint_time` (30 s), skipping `continuous` internal ops (QUIESCE_PATH, QUIESCE_INODE, LOCK_PATH, QUARANTINEDIR_AUTH, QUARANTINE_INODE, QUARANTINEDIR_WORK). Up to `mds_op_log_threshold` (5) ops per check are logged as "slow request X seconds old, received at T: <desc> currently <state>", each doubling its own warn interval; the summary "N slow requests, M included below; oldest blocked for > X secs" is logged at WRN on every tick while N > 0. Metric `SLOW_REQUEST` (10), `MDS_SLOW_REQUEST`, WARN, "N slow requests are blocked > T secs". `mds.slow_reply` separately counts first replies sent >= `mds_op_complaint_time` after receipt.
features.notes: With `mds_enable_op_tracker=false` requests are not registered, so `MDS_SLOW_REQUEST` and the clog lines disappear while `mds.slow_reply` keeps counting.

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO and slow RADOS IO detection
features.summary: Warns when MDS RADOS operations have been outstanding longer than the OSD complaint time.
features.description: Every `MDSIOContextBase` (dirfrag fetch/commit, backtraces, tables, sessionmap, journal pointer, ...) is linked at construction into one process-wide list under a spinlock; `check_ios_in_flight` counts entries older than `now - osd_op_complaint_time` (the OSD option, 30 s), stopping at 100 ("100+"). Metric `SLOW_METADATA_IO` (12), `MDS_SLOW_METADATA_IO`, WARN, "N slow metadata IOs are blocked > T secs, oldest blocked for S secs". The journal write-error handler and the file-size recovery probe are built with `track=false`, so slow file recoveries never raise it.
features.notes: Journal completions are tracked from submit time. See also F-STORE-066 (untracked probes).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: MDS_DAMAGE and MDS_READ_ONLY state warnings
features.summary: Reports a non-empty damage table (HEALTH_ERR) and a read-only rank (HEALTH_WARN).
features.description: Metric `DAMAGE` (8), `MDS_DAMAGE`, HEALTH_ERR, "Metadata damage detected", summary "%num% MDSs report damaged metadata", while the `DamageTable` is non-empty. Metric `READ_ONLY` (9), `MDS_READ_ONLY`, WARN, "MDS in read-only mode", while `mdcache->is_readonly()`. The monitor also emits `MDS_DAMAGE` for ranks in the MDSMap `damaged` set with a different summary; the first summary added wins and MDS metrics are added first.
features.notes: `MDS_DAMAGE` at HEALTH_ERR is not on Rook's ignore list, so it stops the CephFilesystem reconcile (and other gated CRs) while raised. The damage table and read-only mode are owned by category 09-background-services and category 06-journal-and-storage. MDS_DAMAGE detail lines read "mds.<name>(mds.<rank>): Metadata damage detected" and the FSMap damaged-rank detail "fs <name> mds.<rank> is damaged"; both are merged into one check. The alert stays until entries are removed (damage rm, repair) or the daemon restarts. Grafana/Prometheus alerts reference MDS_DAMAGE. See also F-BG-052 (DamageTable), F-STORE-100 (read-only mode).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED
features.summary: Warns when the MDS cache exceeds its memory limit by the health threshold factor.
features.description: Metric `CACHE_OVERSIZED` (11), WARN, when `mds_co` mempool bytes > `mds_cache_memory_limit * mds_health_cache_threshold` (4 GiB x 1.5); message "MDS cache is too large (X/Y); N inodes in use by clients, M stray files" (counts omitted on standby-replay); summary "%num% MDSs report oversized cache". The monitor refuses `mds fail`/`fs fail` for a daemon reporting it unless confirmed.
features.notes: See also F-CACHE-061 (memory-based cache limit).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: MDS_CLIENTS_LAGGY: evictions deferred because of laggy OSDs
features.summary: Reports clients that would have been evicted but were kept because some OSD is laggy.
features.description: With `defer_client_eviction_on_laggy_osds` set and any OSD laggy, `find_idle_sessions` and `evict_cap_revoke_non_responders` skip the evictions of the tick and fill `Server::laggy_clients`; metric `CLIENTS_LAGGY` (13), WARN, "Client C is laggy; not evicted because some OSD(s) is/are laggy" (no metadata), or `CLIENTS_LAGGY_MANY` (14) "Many client (N) are laggy; not evicting since some OSD(s) are laggy" with `client_count`.
features.notes: `mds_metric_summary` has no entry for `CLIENTS_LAGGY_MANY`, so its summary is `???`. See also F-PROTO-047 (eviction deferral).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: MDS_ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME
features.summary: Reports journal replay progress and an estimated remaining time during long replays.
features.description: In `up:replay` (not standby-replay) with replay elapsed time > 30 s (hard-coded), metric `ESTIMATED_REPLAY_TIME` (16), WARN, "replay: P% complete - elapsed time: E, estimated time remaining: R"; summary "%num% estimated journal replay time". The estimate reports 0 elapsed while the read position is still at the trimmed position.
features.notes: The message changes on every tick, so each tick during replay costs a monitor proposal and an MDSMap epoch. Estimate: percent = (read_pos - trimmed_pos) / (write_pos - trimmed_pos) and remaining = (1 - p) / p x elapsed time since the front journal was opened. The `status` command includes `replay_status` {journal_read_pos, journal_write_pos, journal_expire_pos, num_events, num_segments} in replay and standby-replay (F-ADM-032).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: Monitor-derived file-system health checks
features.summary: Checks the monitor computes from the FSMap alone, without MDS input beyond map state.
features.description: `MDSMap::get_health_checks` and `FSMap::get_health_checks` produce `MDS_DAMAGE` (damaged ranks, ERR), `FS_DEGRADED` (failed or damaged ranks, or a daemon in replay..clientreplay, WARN), `MDS_UP_LESS_THAN_MAX` (in < max_mds, WARN), `MDS_ALL_DOWN` (no up ranks and max_mds > 0, ERR), `MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS` (ERR), `FS_INLINE_DATA_DEPRECATED` (WARN), `FS_WITH_FAILED_MDS` (no replacement available, WARN) and `MDS_INSUFFICIENT_STANDBY` (standby + standby-replay < `standby_count_wanted`, WARN). They are merged after the daemon metrics; `%num%`, `%plurals%`, `%isorare%`, `%hasorhave%` placeholders are filled from the detail count.
features.notes: Computed entirely in the unchanged monitor; listed here because operators, Prometheus alerts and Rook's health gate key on these codes. `FSMap::get_health` (legacy "mds X is laggy" summaries) is dead code. `FS_DEGRADED` computes per-rank detail lines and discards them. `MDS_INSUFFICIENT_STANDBY` counts the file system's followers plus the whole shared standby pool, and one shared standby satisfies `standby_count_wanted = 1` on every file system. See also F-CLU-062 (map-side inputs, standby_count_wanted).

legacy_parts.note: MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS (detail 'snapshots possibly created by pre-mimic MDS'); FS_INLINE_DATA_DEPRECATED; the uncalled FSMap::get_health and MDSMap::get_health with their old summary strings such as 'is laggy/unresponsive'. Every MDSMap starts with CEPH_MDSMAP_ALLOW_MULTIMDS_SNAPS set, and the monitor changes that flag only with the MDS-only confirmation --yes-i-am-really-a-mds, so MULTIMDS_WITH_OLDSNAPS arises only for file systems with snapshots from before Mimic. inline_data is enabled only by `fs set <fs> inline_data true --yes-i-really-really-mean-it`, which the monitor answers with a deprecation notice and which no mgr module, cephadm or Rook sends. FSMap::get_health and MDSMap::get_health have no caller; the other checks are computed for current file systems and are keyed on by Rook, alerts and cephadm.
evidence_notes: grep of src/pybind/mgr, src/cephadm and rook/pkg CephFS code: no inline_data setter (Rook matches are RGW placement fields)

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: Health-gated monitor commands
features.summary: Some monitor commands refuse to act while MDS daemons report health metrics.
features.description: `mds fail` and `fs fail` return `-EPERM` with `errmsg_for_unhealthy_mds` if a target daemon reports `MDS_HEALTH_TRIM` or `MDS_HEALTH_CACHE_OVERSIZED`, unless `--yes-i-really-mean-it`. `fs set <fs> max_mds` requires confirmation if any daemon reports any metric; `has_any_health_warning` scans every gid of every file system and counts `MDS_HEALTH_DUMMY` too, so a warning in fs A blocks `fs set B max_mds`.
features.notes: Rook sends `fs set max_mds`, `fs fail` and `mds fail` without the confirmation flag; a refusal aborts its `upgradeMDS` (retried, standby-replay left disabled) and is only logged elsewhere (mgr-tools page section 8).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: Cluster log (clog) messages
features.summary: Operator-facing warnings and errors the MDS sends to the monitors' cluster log.
features.description: 99 `clog` call sites under `src/mds/` on the default `cluster` channel: slow requests, late cap revokes, oldest tid, evictions ("Evicting (and blocklisting) client session N (addr)", "evicting unresponsive client ..."), session denials (missing features, non-allowable root, duplicated uuid), reconnect denials, write and journal errors (each followed by `handle_write_error` or `damaged()`), replay and table load errors, dirfrag and scatter-stat inconsistencies, backtraces, scrub summaries, `force file system read-only`, stopping progress, Mantle fallback. Routing follows `clog_to_monitors`, `clog_to_syslog*`, `clog_to_graylog*` (tracked keys, parsed by `update_log_config`); `damaged()` and `abort()` flush the log to the monitor before exiting.
features.notes: qa tests and log ignorelists match clog wording (e.g. qa/suites/fs/functional/tasks/client-recovery.yaml). The full message catalogue is on the config page section 5.6.

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: Scrub task status in the mgr service map
features.summary: While scrub is not idle, the rank publishes a `scrub status` summary shown under "task status:" in `ceph -s`.
features.description: Every `mds_task_status_update_interval` (2 s) a timer calls `ScrubStack::scrub_summary()`; if not `idle` it sends `{"scrub status": <summary>}` with `MgrClient::service_daemon_update_task_status`, and one empty map when it returns to idle. Summary strings: `idle`, `idle+waiting`, `active`, `aborting`, `pausing`, `paused` (with `+aborting` while an abort is pending), followed by ` paths [<path>,...]`. It rides in `MMgrReport.task_status` (only when dirty); the mgr keys it by peer type `mds` and daemon name and stores it in the service map; the monitor prints it in `ceph -s` and `ceph service dump` shows it.
features.notes: qa polls `ceph status` JSON `servicemap.services.mds.daemons.<name>.task_status["scrub status"]` with `startswith` and expects it to become empty when idle (qa/tasks/ceph_manager.py:3471-3486). See also F-BG-037 (summary strings and scrub status).

features.group: Health, slow operations, cluster log and task status
features.name: In-memory log dump on extraordinary events
features.summary: Optionally dumps the recent in-memory debug log after an eviction, a missed beacon ack or an internal heartbeat miss.
features.description: When `mds_extraordinary_events_dump_interval` is changed at runtime to a non-zero value (0-60 s) while `debug_mds` is below 10 with gather level >= 10, a timer fires every N seconds and, if `client_eviction_dump`, `missed_beacon_ack_dump` or `missed_internal_heartbeat_dump` was set since the last check, calls `dump_recent()` and clears the flags; otherwise the handler resets the option to 0.
features.notes: A configured value is ignored at startup (member hard-coded to 0); each runtime change to a non-zero value schedules a new self-rescheduling timer without cancelling the previous chain (code inspection). Documented in troubleshooting.rst.

features.name: mgr libcephfs connection pool and mount identity
features.summary: mgr modules mount CephFS through pooled libcephfs handles authenticated as the mgr entity and running as uid/gid 0.
features.description: `CephfsConnectionPool.Connection.connect` creates `LibCephFS(rados_inst=mgr.rados)` and sets `client_mount_uid=0`, `client_mount_gid=0`, `client_check_pool_perm=false`, `client_quota=false`, `client_respect_subvolume_snapshot_visibility=false`, `client_fscrypt_as=false` before mounting by fs name; it then registers the mount's addresses with the mgr, which blocklists them for `mon_mgr_blocklist_interval` (1 day) on mgr failover. At most 5 mounts per fs per pool; idle connections (60 s) are closed by a 30 s timer; a connection is reused only while the fscid is unchanged, otherwise torn down with `abort_conn()` (no session close). Separate pools exist for volumes, the cloner, the purge queue, snap_schedule, mirroring and nfs; the dashboard opens un-pooled, unregistered mounts. The MDS therefore sees many concurrent sessions from one `mgr.<id>` entity.
features.notes: Old mgr sessions become blocklisted clients after failover; aborted pooled connections leave sessions to time out on the MDS.

features.name: mgr/volumes: volume lifecycle (fs volume create, rm, rename, ls, info)
features.summary: Creates and removes whole file systems with pools and MDS services; ls/info read sizes through the client protocol.
features.description: `fs volume create` runs `osd pool create cephfs.<name>.meta|.data` (bulk), `fs new`, and orchestrator `apply` of `mds.<name>`; `fs volume rm --yes-i-really-mean-it` checks `mon_allow_pool_delete`, cancels purges, closes pooled mounts, removes the orchestrator service, then `fs fail`, `fs rm`, `osd pool rm`; `fs volume rename` creates the new MDS service, runs `fs rename --yes-i-really-mean-it` (mon requires no MDS up and `refuse_client_session`) and renames pools. `ls`/`info` use `statx(/volumes, SIZE)` (directory size = rbytes) and count `/volumes/_deleting` entries.
features.notes: Without an orchestrator `fs volume rm` only logs a warning and leaves the MDS daemons running. The MDS sees the effects as FSMap changes (`fs fail`, `fs rm`) owned by category 01-cluster-membership-and-ha.

features.name: mgr/volumes: in-filesystem layout, .meta files, versions, user metadata, open side effects
features.summary: mgr/volumes keeps all its state as ordinary files and directories under `/volumes`, so it depends only on POSIX behaviour and vxattrs, not on MDS on-disk formats.
features.description: Layout: `/volumes/<group|_nogroup>/<subvol>/{.meta, <uuid>/ (data root), .trash/<uuid>/ (v2), .snap/}`, `/volumes/_index/clone/<id>` symlinks, `/volumes/_deleting/<uuid>`, `/volumes/_legacy/<md5>.meta`, `/volumes/$<auth_id>.meta`, `/volumes/_<group>:<subvol>.meta`. `.meta` is an INI file rewritten via `<path>.tmp` (`O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC`, 0640), `fsync`, and `rename` over the old file. Every subvolume open re-reads `.meta`, re-applies `setxattr ceph.dir.subvolume 1`, stats the data path and the `_legacy` meta, and runs a stale snapshot metadata cleanup, so even `fs subvolume info` issues an MDS SETXATTR and several lookups/opens/reads. A v1 subvolume without snapshots is upgraded to v2 by rewriting `version = 2`; legacy subvolumes get a `_legacy` meta. `fs subvolume metadata ...` and `fs subvolume snapshot metadata ...` store user key-values in the `[USER_METADATA]` and `[SNAP_METADATA_<snap>]` sections of `.meta`, not in MDS snapshot metadata.
features.notes: v1 marks the `<uuid>` dir as subvolume, v2 the base dir. A crash between writing `.meta.tmp` and the rename leaves a stale tmp file that the next flush truncates.

legacy_parts.note: SubvolumeLoader.upgrade_to_v2_subvolume: a v1 subvolume without snapshots is upgraded to v2 by rewriting `version = 2` in `.meta`. mgr/volumes creates v2 subvolumes from 14.2.12, 15.2.9 and 16.2.0 on, current code creates every subvolume and clone with the maximum version (v2), and the upgrade skips legacy-mode subvolumes, so it runs only on a `<subvolume>/.meta` with version 1 written by an older mgr/volumes. The `_legacy` meta path is not counted here: besides subvolumes created by ceph_volume_client (shipped through 16.2.x), SubvolumeBase.discover enters it for any directory under /volumes/<group> without a valid `.meta`, which a baseline file system can also contain (derived from code).
evidence_notes: git cat-file: versions/subvolume_v2.py absent at v14.2.11 and v15.2.8, present at v14.2.12, v15.2.9 and v16.2.0; src/pybind/ceph_volume_client.py present at v16.2.15, absent at v17.2.0

features.name: mgr/volumes: subvolume groups
features.summary: Groups are directories under `/volumes` with quota, layout, ownership, mode, pins and charmap attributes.
features.description: `fs subvolumegroup create|rm|info|resize|ls|exist|getpath|pin|charmap`: `mkdirs`, `rmdir` (`ENOTEMPTY` reported to callers such as Rook), `stat/statx`, `chown` (default 0:0), `lchmod`, `setxattr ceph.quota.max_bytes`, `ceph.dir.layout.pool` (explicit or the nearest ancestor's, which requires `/` to expose a layout), `ceph.dir.pin*`, `ceph.dir.{casesensitive,normalization,encoding}`, `removexattr ceph.dir.charmap`. `fs subvolumegroup snapshot create` always returns `-ENOSYS`; `rm`/`ls` work on existing group snapshots. Group names equal to an internal dir are rejected.
features.notes: Rook creates group `csi` and any `CephFilesystemSubVolumeGroup` (create, resize `--no-shrink`, `pin distributed 1` by default, rm).

features.name: mgr/volumes: subvolume create
features.summary: Creates a subvolume as a directory tree marked with `ceph.dir.subvolume` and configured through vxattrs and setattr.
features.description: `SubvolumeV2.create`: stat/`mkdirs` the group dir; `mkdirs /volumes/<g>/<s>/<uuid4>`; `setxattr(base_path, ceph.dir.subvolume, 1)`; on the data dir in order `ceph.quota.max_bytes`, `ceph.dir.layout.pool`, then `ceph.dir.layout.pool_namespace=fsvolumens_<group>_<subvol>` (isolated) or a copy of the nearest ancestor's pool, `chown`, `lchmod`, earmark xattr (always written, empty string if none), `ceph.dir.normalization`, `ceph.dir.casesensitive=0`, enctag; then write `.meta` and create the empty auth meta file. Create is idempotent (re-applies attrs if it exists); on error the partial subvolume is moved to trash. Names must match `[A-Za-z0-9-_.]`.
features.notes: Relies on the MDS for: subvolume flag set/get (nested -> `-EINVAL`), layout and quota vxattrs, charmap settable only on an empty directory, a zero-length user xattr round-trip, and a layout on `/`. Subvolume semantics are owned by category 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes.

features.name: mgr/volumes: removal, trash, snapshot retention and asynchronous purge
features.summary: Subvolume removal renames trees into a trash area that background threads delete with ordinary client unlink/rmdir traffic.
features.description: `fs subvolume rm` with snapshots and no `--retain-snapshots` -> `-ENOTEMPTY`; otherwise `rename(/volumes/<g>/<s>, /volumes/_deleting/<uuid4>)` and unlink the auth meta file. With `--retain-snapshots` the `.meta` state becomes `snapshot-retained`, the `<uuid>` dir moves to `<base>/.trash/<uuid>` and a symlink is placed in `_deleting`. 4 purge threads pick `_deleting` entries and run `LibCephFS.rmtree` (Python `openat`/`fdopendir`/`readdir`/`unlinkat` walk); a directory whose `rmdir` fails `ENOTEMPTY` after being emptied is assumed to hold snapshots and left in place.
features.notes: All bulk deletion of subvolume data reaches the MDS as client unlink/rmdir, which creates strays and purge work (category 09-background-services). The trash rename is a cross-directory rename through the shared `/volumes/<g>` and `/volumes/_deleting` dirfrags.

features.name: mgr/volumes: subvolume resize via quota
features.summary: Resizes a subvolume by setting `ceph.quota.max_bytes` and reports usage from directory rbytes.
features.description: `fs subvolume resize <new_size> [--no_shrink]` accepts bytes or `<n>[KMGTPE][i][B]`, `inf`/`infinite` -> 0 (quota removed); with `--no_shrink` a size below `stat().st_size` of the data dir is rejected. Output `[{"bytes_used":N},{"bytes_quota":N},{"bytes_pcent":"x.xx"|"undefined"}]`. `bytes_used` everywhere (`info`, `resize`, `volume info`) is directory `st_size`, which libcephfs fills from `rstat.rbytes` (`client_dirsize_rbytes` true).

features.name: mgr/volumes: subvolume and group pinning
features.summary: Sets export pins on subvolume base dirs or group dirs through vxattrs.
features.description: `fs subvolume pin <export|distributed|random> <setting>` sets `ceph.dir.pin` (int), `ceph.dir.pin.distributed` (bool -> 0/1) or `ceph.dir.pin.random` (float) on `base_path` (groups: the group dir). MDS validation: pin rank >= 256 -> `-EDOM`, negative unsets; `pin.random` outside [0,1] -> `-EDOM`, above `mds_export_ephemeral_random_max` -> `-EINVAL`; root -> `-EINVAL`.
features.notes: Rook pins every `CephFilesystemSubVolumeGroup` (`distributed 1` by default). Pinning semantics belong to category 07-multi-mds. Commands: `ceph fs subvolumegroup pin <vol> <group> <export|distributed|random> <setting>` and `ceph fs subvolume pin <vol> <sub> <export|distributed|random> <setting> [<group>]`; the setting is converted with int(), int(strtobool()) or float() (EINVAL "pin value wrong type" on failure) and set through the mgr's libcephfs handle on /volumes/<group> or /volumes/<group|_nogroup>/<subvol> (not the inner UUID data directory), passing MDS errors back unchanged. The _nogroup group cannot be pinned (EPERM); the mgr never reads pins back. With a distributed group pin, subvolumes are spread by the group directory's dirfrags (a hash of their names), not one rank per subvolume. Rook's CephFilesystemSubVolumeGroup controller applies `distributed 1` when the CR has no pinning spec (rook pkg/daemon/ceph/client/subvolumegroup.go); doc/cephfs/fs-volumes.rst documents `ceph fs subvolumegroup pin cephfilesystem-a csi distributed 1`; qa uses `subvolumegroup pin cephfs qa random 0.20` with mds_export_ephemeral_random_max 0.20. See also F-MULTI-038, F-MULTI-045, F-MULTI-046 (pin vxattrs). See also F-MULTI-038 (ceph.dir.pin).

features.name: mgr/volumes: charmap (case sensitivity, normalization, encoding)
features.summary: Sets and removes per-directory name handling attributes on subvolume data dirs and group dirs.
features.description: `fs subvolume charmap set|get|rm`: `setxattr ceph.dir.<casesensitive|normalization|encoding>` then `getxattr ceph.dir.charmap`; rm = `removexattr ceph.dir.charmap`. The MDS requires the directory to be empty and without snapshots (`-ENOTEMPTY`), refuses charmap on root or a non-dir, and refuses setting `ceph.dir.charmap` itself (`-EINVAL`, only removal). Create therefore applies normalization and case sensitivity before anything is created in the data dir.
features.notes: See also F-NS-075 (charmap).

features.name: mgr/volumes and mgr/nfs: earmark and enctag xattrs
features.summary: Plain user xattrs that tag a subvolume's intended consumer (nfs, smb) and encryption tag.
features.description: `user.ceph.subvolume.earmark` (valid: empty, `nfs[.x...]`, `smb`, `smb.cluster.<id>`; clear = set `""`) and `user.ceph.subvolume.enctag` (max 255 chars) are read and written with getxattr/setxattr. Create always writes the earmark, empty if none, as a set with a zero-length value, so volumes relies on the MDS storing and returning zero-length user xattr values. mgr/nfs checks the earmark at export creation, sets `nfs` if empty and refuses with `-EAGAIN` if it belongs to another scope.
features.notes: `get_earmark` catches `OSError` but libcephfs raises `cephfs.NoData`, so a missing xattr surfaces as `EarmarkException(EFAULT)`, which `info` and the NFS resolver treat as no earmark.

features.name: mgr/volumes: subvolume snapshots
features.summary: Subvolume snapshots are `mkdir`/`rmdir`/`readdir` in the `.snap` directory of the directory carrying `ceph.dir.subvolume`.
features.description: Create refuses a name used by a group snapshot, then `mkdir(<snapbase>/<name>, 0755)` (MKSNAP; `EEXIST` treated as success); remove `-EAGAIN` with pending clones, drops snapshot metadata from `.meta`, then `rmdir` (RMSNAP); list filters names starting with `_` (inherited `_<name>_<ino>` entries); info reads `ceph.snap.btime` as `created_at` and `ceph.dir.layout.pool`. MDS rules relied on: `allow_new_snaps` unset -> `-EPERM`, uid range -> `-EPERM`, caps `s`, mksnap below a subvolume root -> `-EPERM`, `mds_max_snaps_per_dir` reached -> `-EMLINK`, duplicate -> `-EEXIST`, empty, `_`-prefixed or > 240-byte names -> `-EINVAL`.
features.notes: Adding a mirror checkpoint (`SNAP_METADATA`) changes `snapinfo.stamp` and therefore the `ceph.snap.btime` reported as `created_at`. See also F-SNAP-013 (mksnap).

features.name: mgr/volumes: snapshot visibility
features.summary: Controls whether `.snap` is visible in a subvolume through `ceph.dir.subvolume.snaps.visible`.
features.description: `fs subvolume snapshot_visibility set|get` accepts `true`/`false` and sets the vxattr on `base_path`, and also on the data dir if it has a quota (own snaprealm). The MDS handler is a no-op returning 0 when the inode has no snaprealm, and GETVXATTR returns an empty value then.
features.notes: The mgr's own mounts set `client_respect_subvolume_snapshot_visibility=false` and always see `.snap`. See also F-SNAP-055 (snaps.visible vxattr).

features.name: mgr/volumes: snapshot clone
features.summary: Copies a snapshot into a new subvolume with a client-side tree copy in background threads.
features.description: Clone creates the destination like a subvolume (attrs copied from the snapshot: uid/gid/mode, layout pool and namespace, earmark, normalization, casesensitive, enctag, `ceph.fscrypt.auth|file`), writes `.meta` with state `pending`, symlinks `/volumes/_index/clone/<id>` to it and records the track id in the source `.meta`. `max_concurrent_clones` cloner threads pick the symlink with the smallest `st_ctime` (readlink truncated to `st_size`), copy with `LibCephFS.cptree` (dirs, regular files, symlinks; 1 MiB reads/writes, `fsync` per file, attrs via `*at` calls), then copy `ceph.quota.max_bytes|max_files`. Progress uses `ceph.dir.rbytes`/`rentries` of the snapshot and destination; state transitions go through `.meta`.
features.notes: Relies on symlink `st_size` == target length, meaningful symlink ctime ordering, rstat of snapshot inodes and readable snapshot data. Quota is applied only after the copy.

features.name: mgr/volumes: fs subvolume evict
features.summary: Evicts all clients of one cephx id that mounted a given subvolume, on every up rank.
features.description: `SubvolumeV1.evict` builds filters `["auth_name=<id>", "client_metadata.root=<data path>"]` and starts one `RankEvicter` thread per `mdsmap.up` entry; each waits (poll 5 s, ~35 s max) for `up:active` or `up:clientreplay` and sends `session evict` by gid on the module's mounted handle, retrying while it returns `-ETIMEDOUT`. Any other error returns `-EINVAL` to the user, a wait timeout `-ETIMEDOUT`.
features.notes: `client_metadata.root` is matched exactly, so a client that mounted a subdirectory or reports a trailing slash is not evicted. The global `GlobalLock` is held for the whole command, so an unresponsive MDS stalls all volumes commands.

features.name: mgr/volumes: fs quiesce
features.summary: Quiesces a set of subvolumes through the quiesce-db leader.
features.description: `fs quiesce <vol> [members...] [--set-id ...] [--leader] [--with_leader <gid>]` maps each member `[<group>/]<subvol>[?query]` to its data path and sends `quiesce db` with `roots` plus the whole command dict to `mdsmap.qdb_leader` (or `--with_leader`) with `one_shot`, up to 5 attempts, following `{"leader": <gid>}` on `-ENOTTY`. Output is returned verbatim. The global lock is released before the tell.
features.notes: `qdb_leader` is chosen by the monitor (`MDSMonitor::assign_quiesce_db_leader`). Members are resolved to the subvolume data path with GETPATH (URL syntax keeps scheme, authority and query); the command is sent with libcephfs mds_command2 (one_shot, so a connection reset gives EPIPE); extra keys (vol_name, members, group_name, leader, with_leader) are ignored by the MDS parser; --leader only prints mds.<gid>. If qdb_leader is 0 (no active rank) the mgr targets "mds.0", which libcephfs may resolve as rank 0 (src/client/Client.cc:6697-6720). qa/tasks/quiescer.py uses the same ENOTTY redirect. See also F-QOS-053 (quiesce db).

features.name: mgr/volumes: subvolume quarantine
features.summary: Enables or disables quarantine of a subvolume without opening it.
features.description: `fs subvolume quarantine enable|disable` sends `quarantine enable|disable path=/volumes/<group|_nogroup>/<sub>` to the first `up:active`/`up:clientreplay` MDS in sorted `mdsmap.up` order and returns rc and JSON. It takes no lock and does not open the subvolume because its mount lacks quarantine access. `fs subvolume info` returns `{"name","group","quarantine":"enabled"}` when opening fails with `-EACCES`.
features.notes: The command needs perm rw and builds the path without opening the subvolume. When opening fails with -EACCES, fs subvolume info returns success with only {name, group, "quarantine": "enabled"} (any other -EACCES cause is reported the same way), and on success it adds "quarantine": "disabled". The mgr's own client (allow *, quarantine-aware) gets -EACCES inside quarantined subvolumes, so getpath, rm, resize and snapshot create and list fail while subvolume ls stays complete. The call works only when the chosen rank is auth for the subvolume root (otherwise -EXDEV; the code comment that the MDS forwards is wrong). Legacy v1 subvolumes carry ceph.dir.subvolume on <uuid>, so the command gets -EINVAL for them (inferred). The MDS offers no status query other than dump inode. snap_schedule and other modules using libcephfs get -EACCES on quarantined subvolumes (inferred). See also F-QOS-058 (MDS command).

features.name: mgr/snap_schedule: scheduled snapshots and retention
features.summary: Takes periodic snapshots with `mkdir` in `.snap` and prunes them, storing its schedule DB in the metadata pool.
features.description: Commands `fs snap-schedule status|list|add|remove|retention add|remove|activate|deactivate`; per schedule a timer does `mkdir(<path>/<client_snapdir>/scheduled-<YYYY-mm-dd-HH_MM_SS_UTC>, 0755)`; pruning lists `.snap`, keeps `scheduled-` names per retention spec (`n m h d w M y`) capped at `mds_max_snaps_per_dir - 1`, and `rmdir`s the rest. Its SQLite DB lives in the CephFS metadata pool (default namespace) as striped objects `snap_db_v0.db.<16 hex>` and `snap_db_v0.db-journal.<16 hex>` with `striper.*` xattrs and lock; a legacy object `snap_db_v0` in namespace `cephfs-snap-schedule` is imported once and deleted.
features.notes: For v2 subvolumes the schedule path is `<data dir>/..`, resolved with LOOKUPPARENT when the parent dentry is not cached. Rook adds schedules and polls `fs snap-schedule status` when mirroring is configured.

legacy_parts.note: One-time import and removal of the legacy dump object `snap_db_v0` in RADOS namespace `cephfs-snap-schedule` of the metadata pool (SnapSchedClient.get_schedule_db). snap_schedule in Ceph 16.2.x and earlier stored its schedule DB as the dump object snap_db_v0 (ioctx.write_full); from 17.2.0 the module stores the DB in libcephsqlite objects and only reads and removes the old object. The current module never writes the dump object, so a metadata pool created at the baseline never holds it.
evidence_notes: git de8b110f9f7 'pybind/mgr/snap_schedule: use ceph VFS' (first tag v17.1.0)
grep of src/pybind/mgr/snap_schedule: no write of SNAP_DB_OBJECT_NAME at this commit

features.name: mgr/mirroring: enable, peers, bootstrap and directory distribution
features.summary: Configures snapshot mirroring, stores its state in the metadata pool and marks peer roots with `ceph.mirror.info`.
features.description: Enable creates RADOS object `cephfs_mirror` (metadata pool, default namespace) and runs `fs mirror enable`. Peer add mounts the remote fs, refuses mirroring back, and sets `ceph.mirror.info = "cluster_id=<uuid> fs_id=<int>"` with `XATTR_CREATE` on the remote root (`-EEXIST` with a different value -> refused); peer remove clears it. Bootstrap create runs `fs authorize <fs> client.<name> / rwps` and returns a base64 token. Directory assignment lives in `cephfs_mirror` omap (`dir_map_<path>`, `instance_<id>`, `sync_stat/...`); the module notifies `cephfs_mirror.<instance_id>` objects every 1 s and blocklists instances that stop acking (`osd blocklist add`).
features.notes: MDS side: `ceph.mirror.info` only on root (`-EINVAL` elsewhere), stored as raw xattrs `ceph.mirror.info.cluster_id`/`.fs_id`, which the client synthesizes into the value. Mirroring-enabled file systems cannot be renamed (`-EPERM`). See also F-NS-070 (ceph.mirror xattrs).

features.name: mgr/mirroring: checkpoints through snapshot metadata
features.summary: Records mirror checkpoint status as key/value metadata on snapshots using the `SNAP_METADATA` op.
features.description: Checkpoint commands list `<dir>/.snap` (skipping `_` names), read `snap_info()` (id and metadata from the client's cached `snapid` and `snap_metadata`), choose the highest snap id as latest and write keys `cephfs.mirror.checkpoint.{status,created_at,updated_at,error_msg}` with `do_snap_md_op(path, key, val, CREATE|EXCL)` or `REMOVE`, i.e. `CEPH_MDS_OP_SNAP_METADATA` (0x1406) with payload `string key, string value, u32 flag` (CREATE 1, EXCL 2, REMOVE 4). MDS errors: `-ENOTDIR`, `-EPERM` (uid range), `-EINVAL` (empty/`_` key, EXCL on existing, REMOVE of missing, bad flag), `-ENOENT` (no such snapshot), `-EBADMSG`; success is journaled through the snap table (`prepare_update` + `EUpdate`).
features.notes: The op is not caps-checked (see F-ADM-013) and carries the `CEPH_MDS_OP_WRITE` bit, so a read-only MDS returns `-EROFS`. See also F-SNAP-017 (SNAP_METADATA).

features.name: mgr/stats: fs perf stats (and cephfs-top)
features.summary: Aggregated per-client and per-subvolume performance metrics collected by rank 0 through MDS perf-metric queries, plus client metadata from `client ls`.
features.description: The stats module registers three MDS perf queries (`add_mds_perf_query`): per-rank client keys (`mds_rank`, `client_id` regex `^(client.<id>\s+<ip>):.*`), subvolume keys (`mds_rank`, `subvolume_path`) with counters 16-21, and global client keys with counters 0-15; the mgr sends them in `MMgrConfigure`, rank 0's `MetricAggregator` answers in `MMgrReport.metric_report_message` with `client_id` formatted as `stringify(entity_inst_t)`. Queries expire after 1 min and are re-registered when the rank-0 gid becomes active. It sends `client ls` to every daemon with rank 0 and reads `id`, `client_metadata.hostname`, `.root`, optional `.mount_point`, `.kernel_version`, and `metric_spec.metric_flags.feature_bits` (hex, bit i = counter i supported). `cephfs-top` (identity `client.fstop`) calls `fs perf stats` and requires output `version == 2`; it indexes counters positionally in `global_counters` order.
features.notes: Only rank 0 aggregates; libcephfs sends global metrics only to rank 0 when it advertises `CEPHFS_FEATURE_METRIC_COLLECT`; the kclient picks the lowest open session with that bit, so kclient metrics may arrive at another rank and be forwarded via `MMDSMetrics`. The kclient enum uses bit 22 for subvolume metrics while the C++ MDS assigns bit 22 to `CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP`. Metric semantics belong to category 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine. A missing required client ls key raises KeyError in the module. A client with no session on rank 0 is missing from client_metadata and global_metrics even if another rank receives its metrics. subvolume_metrics entries are never culled while the user query lives. Output version 2 holds the 16 global counter names, per-client metadata (valid_metrics from the client's metric_spec), global_metrics, per-rank metrics with delayed_ranks and subvolume_metrics. See also F-QOS-028, F-QOS-029, F-QOS-030 (MDS side of perf queries).

features.name: mgr/status: fs status
features.summary: Prints per-rank state, activity rates, dentry/inode counts and versions from mgr-held counters and MDS metadata.
features.description: `fs status` reads `mds_mem.dn`, `mds_mem.ino`, `mds_mem.dir`, `mds_mem.cap`, `mds_sessions.session_count` (rank 0, else another rank), the rate of `mds_server.handle_client_request` ("Reqs: N/s") for active ranks, the rate of `mds_log.replayed` ("Evts: N/s") for standby-replay, and `ceph_version` from `mds metadata` (the boot beacon `sys_info`). These counters reach the mgr because their priorities are >= 5.

features.name: mgr/dashboard: CephFS pages
features.summary: Dashboard CephFS pages read counters, list and evict clients, authorize users and browse files through its own libcephfs mounts.
features.description: Counters `mds_server.handle_client_request`, `mds_log.ev`, `mds_cache.num_strays`, `mds.exported`, `mds.exported_inodes`, `mds.imported`, `mds.imported_inodes`, `mds.inodes`, `mds.caps`, `mds.subtrees`, `mds_mem.ino`; `session ls` (format json) and `client evict` with `filters=["id=<n>"]` to `<fscid>:0`; `fs authorize` (optionally `root_squash`). File browser via un-pooled `LibCephFS`: `opendir/readdir`, `mkdirs`, `rmdir`, snapshots with `mkdir/rmdir` in the snapdir, quotas via `ceph.quota.max_bytes|max_files`, `ceph.dir.rbytes|rfiles|rsubdirs`, `rename`, file create/write and `unlink`; volume, subvolume, schedule and mirror pages call other modules.
features.notes: `mds.exported`/`mds.imported` are DEBUGONLY and `mds_log.replay` does not exist, so those series are empty.

features.name: mgr/prometheus: MDS and file-system metadata metrics
features.summary: Exports MDS metadata, file-system metadata and health check codes as Prometheus series.
features.description: `ceph_mds_metadata{ceph_daemon="mds.<name>", fs_id, hostname, public_addr, rank, ceph_version}` (standbys with `fs_id="-1"`), `ceph_fs_metadata{data_pools, fs_id, metadata_pool, name}` and `ceph_health_detail{name=<check code>, severity}`; perf counters only with `exclude_perf_counters=false` (default true). influx and telegraf modules export unlabeled counters with prio >= 5.
features.notes: The values come from the FSMap and the boot beacon metadata (`hostname`, `ceph_version`), i.e. from beacons owned by category 01-cluster-membership-and-ha.

features.name: mgr/telemetry: MDS data collection
features.summary: Opt-in telemetry reports file-system sizes from counters, MDS metadata counts and, optionally, MDS heap and mempool data.
features.description: Basic channel: sums per file system of `mds_sessions.session_count`, `mds_mem.ino|dn|cap`, `mds.subtrees`, and rank 0 `mds.root_rfiles|root_rbytes|root_rsnaps`; `gather_mds_metadata` counts `mds metadata` keys (`ceph_version`, `arch`, `os`, `cpu`). Perf channel: every reported counter; with the `perf_memory_metrics` collection, `heap stats` (12 integers after "tcmalloc heap stats") and `dump_mempools` per MDS; errors are only logged.

features.name: mgr/mds_autoscaler
features.summary: Keeps the orchestrator's MDS daemon count at `max_mds + standby_count_wanted`; it never talks to the MDS.
features.description: On each FSMap notification, for each fs with an orchestrator service `mds.<fs_name>` that has `placement.count`, it applies `count = max_mds + standby_count_wanted` with `apply_mds`.
features.notes: During a cephadm upgrade the `fs set max_mds 1` step makes it shrink and later regrow the service; nothing coordinates the two.

features.name: mgr/nfs: CephFS exports
features.summary: Creates NFS-Ganesha exports of CephFS paths with dedicated cephx users and earmark checks.
features.description: Export creation validates the path is a directory (`statx(path, MODE)` on a pooled mount), checks or sets the `user.ceph.subvolume.earmark` (`nfs`), creates the per-export cephx user, and writes the Ganesha `FSAL { name = CEPH; user_id; filesystem; secret_access_key; cmount_path; ... }` block into RADOS objects in the `.nfs` pool. cephadm's Ganesha config sets `Delegations = false` and `RecoveryBackend = "rados_cluster"`.
features.notes: What Ganesha itself requires from the MDS (reclaim, `ceph_ll_*`) belongs to category 02-client-sessions-and-protocol.

features.name: cephadm MDS deployment
features.summary: cephadm deploys MDS daemons as containers with a fixed command line, keyring location, caps and `mds_join_fs`.
features.description: Service spec `mds.<service_id>` (volumes uses the fs name); daemon id `<service_id>.<host>.<6 random letters>`; keyring `mds.<id>` with `mon 'profile mds'`, `osd 'allow rw tag cephfs *=*'`, `mds 'allow'`; `config set mds.<service_id> mds_join_fs <service_id>`. Container: entrypoint `/usr/bin/ceph-mds`, args `-n mds.<id> -f --setuser ceph --setgroup ceph --default-log-to-file=false` plus journald or stderr logging flags; env `TCMALLOC_MAX_TOTAL_THREAD_CACHE_BYTES=134217728`; mounts the daemon dir at `/var/lib/ceph/mds/ceph-<id>` (keyring inside), the config at `/etc/ceph/ceph.conf` and the run dir for the admin socket. `get_active_daemon` picks a daemon `up:active` in any MDSMap; stray detection compares the mgr's `list_servers()` (hostnames from `mds metadata`) with managed daemons.
features.notes: The `cephfs` pool tag in the osd cap limits the MDS's RADOS access to pools whose application metadata is `cephfs` (set by `fs new`/`fs add_data_pool`). cephadm also gives the mgr `mds 'allow *'` and cephfs-mirror `mds 'allow r'`. See also F-CLU-031 (mds_join_fs).

features.name: cephadm MDS upgrade choreography
features.summary: cephadm reduces each file system to one active rank (or fails it) before redeploying MDS daemons with a new image.
features.description: `_prepare_for_mds_upgrade`: clear `allow_standby_replay`, then either `fs set max_mds 1` and wait until only rank 0 is in with at most one up daemon (default), or with `fail_fs=true` `fs fail` all ranks at once; per daemon, if the service has more daemons than `max_mds`, wait for mon `mds ok-to-stop` (`-EBUSY` if any fs is degraded or too few standbys). After redeploy, `ceph versions` is checked (field 2 of `"ceph version X ..."`), then `max_mds` is restored (or `joinable` set and up to 600 s waited for all ranks active) and `allow_standby_replay` re-enabled.
features.notes: A `ceph_version` string with fewer than three space-separated fields would raise `IndexError` in the upgrade loop. The reaction to `max_mds 1` (rank stopping) and `fs fail` is owned by category 01-cluster-membership-and-ha. See also F-CLU-018 (upgradeable file systems).

features.name: Rook operator: MDS pods, command line, keyring, config and probes
features.summary: Rook runs MDS daemons as Deployments named `<fs>-<letter>` and observes them only through mon commands, the FSMap and a liveness probe.
features.description: Per CephFilesystem Rook creates `activeCount` daemons (doubled with `activeStandby`), entity `mds.<fs>-<letter>` with `mon 'allow profile mds'`, `osd 'allow *'`, `mds 'allow'`, sets `mds_join_fs` and `mds_cache_memory_limit` in the config DB on every reconcile, and starts `ceph-mds` (via `PATH`) with `--fsid`, `--keyring=/etc/ceph/keyring-store/keyring`, `--default-log-*` flags, `--mon-host`, `--mon-initial-members`, `--id=<fs>-<letter>`, `--setuser/--setgroup ceph`, `--foreground` and `--public-addr=<pod IP>` (pod network); `mds_data` is a fresh emptyDir. The only default probe is liveness: `ceph fs dump` as the MDS entity, passing if the name is in `standbys[]` or the fs's `mdsmap.info[]` (or if the command fails); 5 failures 30 s apart restart the container. No readiness, startup or asok probe for the MDS. A per-node ceph-exporter reads sockets in `/run/ceph`; a log-collector sidecar sends `SIGHUP`; stop is `SIGTERM`.
features.notes: Facts from rook v1.21.0 (f190ca3b45f1), cited as rook/pkg/operator/ceph/file/mds/*.go on the mgr-tools page section 3.9; the mgr `rook` module maps `apply_mds` to the `CephFilesystem` CR. Rook never sends any command to the MDS itself and never parses MDS asok or tell output. The liveness probe, the upgrade steps and the `ceph status` check match the FSMap daemon name against the `--id` value.

features.name: Rook operator: upgrade order, ok-to-stop gate and health gating
features.summary: Rook upgrades MDS daemons through `max_mds 1` and pod scale-down, and stops reconciling while certain HEALTH_ERR checks are raised.
features.description: Version check: each `ceph versions` key under `mds` is parsed with `ceph version (\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)` plus build number and commit; an MDS older than the image (lower X.Y.Z, or same with lower build or different commit) triggers `upgradeMDS`: `allow_standby_replay false`, `standby_count_wanted 0`, `mds fail` standby-replay daemons, `max_mds 1`, wait for one up rank, scale other Deployments to 0, update rank 0, then restore. Every Deployment update runs `mds ok-to-stop <letter>` (only the degraded-fs test applies because the bare letter matches no daemon) and a continue check on `ceph status` `fsmap.by_rank[]`, 11 attempts 15 s apart. The reconcile proceeds only on HEALTH_OK/WARN or if every HEALTH_ERR is in {`MDS_ALL_DOWN`, `MGR_MODULE_ERROR`, `AUTH_INSECURE_SERVICE_KEY_TYPE`, `AUTH_INSECURE_ROTATING_SERVICE_KEY_TYPE`, `AUTH_INSECURE_SERVICE_TICKETS`}.
features.notes: A `ceph_version` not matching `ceph version X.Y.Z` (including `unknown`) fails every reconcile; a mismatch makes every reconcile repeat the upgrade sequence. `MDS_DAMAGE` and `MDS_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH` (HEALTH_ERR) are not on the ignore list. Unconfirmed `fs set max_mds`, `fs fail`, `mds fail` are refused while MDS health metrics are raised (F-ADM-083). See also F-CLU-052 (orchestration helpers).

features.name: cephfs-mirror daemon
features.summary: Replicates snapshots of mirrored directories to a remote file system using ordinary libcephfs calls plus snapdiff, blockdiff, flock and snapshot metadata.
features.description: Learns mirrored file systems from its FSMap subscription; per fs it mounts as uid/gid 0, watches `cephfs_mirror` and its own `cephfs_mirror.<instance_id>` object in the metadata pool, and per directory takes `flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)` on the remote dir root (`-EWOULDBLOCK` = owned by another daemon). Sync: get/set `ceph.mirror.dirty_snap_id` on the remote root; incremental via `READDIR_SNAPDIFF` (0x1404) and `FILE_BLOCKDIFF` (0x1405, client requires `CEPHFS_FEATURE_BLOCKDIFF` = 23) or a full crawl; writes with `mkdirat`, `openat`, `pwritev`, `ftruncate`, `symlinkat`, `unlinkat`, `*at` attr calls; `ceph_sync_fs` (`REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG`); then `ceph_mksnap` with metadata `primary_snap_id`; propagates rmsnap and renamesnap; checkpoints on the primary via `SNAP_METADATA`.
features.notes: Deployed with `mds 'allow r'` (cephadm and Rook), relying on SNAP_METADATA not being caps-checked. The snapdiff/blockdiff ops are owned by category 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes.

features.name: Offline journal and table tools (cephfs-journal-tool, cephfs-table-tool)
features.summary: Disaster-recovery tools that read and write the C++ MDS journal and table formats directly in RADOS.
features.description: `cephfs-journal-tool --rank=<fs>:<rank>|<fs>:all [--journal=mdlog|purge_queue]` with `journal inspect|import|export|reset`, `header get|set|recover`, `event get|recover_dentries|splice`: reads the `JournalPointer` (`400.00000000`-style objects of ino `0x400+rank`), journal objects of ino `0x200+rank` (backup `0x300+rank`, purge queue `0x500+rank`), writes dirfrag omap keys `<dname>_<snapid|head>`, `fnode` headers, `<ino>.00000000.inode` and `mds<rank>_inotable`; refuses with `-EPERM` only if the parsed rank is active (rank 0 for `<fs>:all`). `cephfs-table-tool <all|rank> reset|show session|snap|inode` and `take_inos` read/write `mds<rank>_sessionmap`, `mds<rank>_inotable`, `mds_snaptable`, with no online check.
features.notes: Bound to the C++ on-disk encodings (Journaler header, `LogEvent`/`EMetaBlob`, `InodeStore`, `SessionMapStore`, `InoTable`, `SnapServer`); they cannot operate unchanged on a different format. Both read `mds_log_segment_size` / `mds_sessionmap_keys_per_op`.

features.name: Offline data and metadata repair tools (cephfs-data-scan, cephfs-meta-injection, first-damage.py)
features.summary: Tools that rebuild or patch metadata from data-pool backtraces and dirfrag omap values in the C++ formats.
features.description: `cephfs-data-scan init|scan_extents|scan_inodes|scan_links|scan_frags|cleanup|pg_files` reads every data object's `parent` (backtrace), `layout` and `symlink` xattrs written by the C++ MDS, accumulates size/mtime with `cls_cephfs`, injects dentries and inodes into dirfrags, recreates root (`1.00000000.inode`), mdsdir and `lost+found` (ino 4) and updates InoTable/SnapServer; `pg_files` uses libcephfs only. `cephfs-meta-injection listc|showm|showfn|amend|amendfn` edits dirfrag omap values and headers; `first-damage.py` scans dentry omap values for bad `first` snapids against `mds_snaptable` (requires encoding version byte 5). None checks for running MDS daemons.
features.notes: qa test_data_scan.py, test_damage.py and test_meta_injection.py exercise these tools against the C++ formats.

features.name: Client-side tools: cephfs-tool bench and cephfs-shell
features.summary: Userspace tools that use only libcephfs and therefore only the client protocol.
features.description: `cephfs-tool bench` uses `ceph_ll_create/open`, non-blocking readv/writev, `fsync`, `mkdir`, `unlink`, `statfs` and client perf counters. `cephfs-shell` provides an interactive shell with `du` via `ceph.dir.rbytes`, quotas via `ceph.quota.max_bytes|max_files`, snapshots via `mkdir` in `client_snapdir`, arbitrary `setxattr`/`getxattr` and `statfs`.
